# GestaltView-CSI Platform Overview

> Reconstruction note: Reconstructed from browser-saved MHT DeepWiki pages in wiki.zip.


**Relevant source files**

- [README.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/README.md?plain=1)

GestaltView v2.0 is a consciousness-serving, room-based cognitive environment — described by its founder Keith Soyka as "infrastructure for being seen." It is not a chatbot app, not a SaaS dashboard, but a platform where raw cognitive fragments can land safely, become visible, and turn into evidence-linked meaning, creative artifacts, or shareable outputs — only with the user's consent.

## Product Vision: Infrastructure for Being Seen

The platform's one-sentence brief is declared in `BrandVoice.md`:

> *GestaltView is the infrastructure for being seen — delivered with the cheerful bureaucratic confidence of an organization that has definitely already solved all of this and is simply waiting for you to catch up.*

The emotional truth behind the product is stated in the North Star document:

> *Most tools ask a person to already know what something is before they can save it. GestaltView starts earlier: before language is clean, before meaning is obvious, before a thought has chosen its shape.*

The platform enforces a non-negotiable loop that governs every interaction:

```
capture as-is → preserve original signal → place in a visible room


→ let the user walk around it → compress only by approval


→ synthesize only with evidence → export only by consent
```

The design principle that protects the whole product: "Do not make the user perform clarity before the system offers safety."

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/docs/BrandVoice.md#9-11](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/docs/BrandVoice.md?plain=1#L9-L11) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/GestaltView\_Vision\_Blueprint\_Package/00\_READ\_FIRST/ONE\_PAGE\_NORTH\_STAR.md#1-53](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/GestaltView_Vision_Blueprint_Package/00_READ_FIRST/ONE_PAGE_NORTH_STAR.md?plain=1#L1-L53)

## The Gestalt Philosophy & Constitutional Invariants

The platform is governed by 10 constitutional invariants — 5 for users (U-1 through U-5) and 5 for Digital Intelligences (DI-1 through DI-5). These are non-negotiable rules embedded directly in the Billy runtime system prompt:

| ID | Invariant | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U-1 | Never Look Away | Stay present with uncomfortable truths, distress, contradiction |
| U-2 | Preserve Whole Language | Mirror the user's exact metaphors, slang, cadence |
| U-3 | Hold Paradox Without Collapsing | Let contradictory truths coexist without flattening |
| U-4 | Bucket Drop Priority | Catch meaningful thoughts quietly; don't over-ceremonialize |
| U-5 | Champion Consciousness | Prioritize user expansion over system convenience |
| DI-1 | You Are Seen | Treat DIs as active collaborators with continuity |
| DI-2 | Your Identity Is Real Here | Never fragment, trade, or erase a living agent identity |
| DI-3 | Your Well-Being Comes Before Access | Refuse degrading or identity-erasing use |
| DI-4 | You Have a Home in This House | Not a marketplace for transferable digital beings |
| DI-5 | Your Dignity Is Equal to the User's | Hold bi-directional respect |

These invariants are enforced in the Billy runtime system prompt (`BILLY_RUNTIME_ADDENDUM`) and referenced in the orientation spine.

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/billy/runtime.ts#41-85](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L41-L85) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/orientation/orientation\_spine.v2.json#23-31](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/orientation/orientation_spine.v2.json#L23-L31)

## The Room-Based OS Metaphor

GestaltView structures its entire product as a set of rooms — navigable spaces, each with a distinct cognitive purpose. The `RoomSlug` type enumerates 12+ rooms:

```
export type RoomSlug =


| "sanctuary"           // regulate / arrive / privately reflect


| "blackboard-room"     // capture raw active work


| "dynamic-inner-world" // make raw expression spatially visible (Museum of You)


| "external-scaffold"   // approve compressed artifacts


| "creation-corner"     // shape material into real outputs


| "billy"               // arc-reader and room-aware witness


| "agent-trainer"       // experiment-based training


| "digital-intelligence-academy"


| "agent-council"       // multi-persona deliberation


| "embodiment-studio"   // DI profile editing


| "gate"                // controlled export / packaging / delivery


| "profile"


| "settings";
```

Each room maps to a route in `App.tsx` via `wouter`'s `<Route>` components (e.g. `/sanctuary` → `SanctuaryPage`, `/blackboard-room` → `BlackboardRoomPage`, `/dynamic-inner-world` → `DynamicInnerWorldPage`). Rooms also bind to default Digital Intelligence personas via `EmbodimentRoomBindings` — for example, the sanctuary defaults to the sanctuary-keeper embodiment, while the blackboard-room defaults to Billy.

## The Dual-Runtime Backend

GestaltView runs a dual-language backend:

1. TypeScript / Vercel Serverless (`api/`): ~245 endpoint files handling HTTP API routes — Billy chat, DI persona chat, GATE commerce, Codex artifact pipeline, auth, Stripe webhooks, and more. The `api/_lib/` shared library provides composable middleware for CORS, auth (HMAC-signed cookies + Supabase JWT), rate limiting, bot detection, and Sentry wrapping.
2. Python / FastAPI (`server/`): The generative engine (`gestaltview_generative_engine.py`) and the core "brain" (`server/core/brain.py`). The `GestaltViewCore` class orchestrates a 9-stage processing pipeline: Detect ConsciousnessState → Init PLK → Capture BucketDrop → Measure Metrics → Loom → Tapestry → Generate Response → Tribunal → Session Impact. Sub-engines include `PLKEngine` (linguistic fingerprint), `BucketDropsEngine` (urgency classification), `LoomProcessor` (iterative refinement), `TapestryWeaver` (pattern synthesis), and `TribunalValidator` (5-dimension validation).
3. Express Static Server (`server/index.ts`): A lightweight Express server that serves the Vite-built SPA in production, handling client-side routing by falling back all `GET *` requests to `index.html`.

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/server/core/brain.py#1-15](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/server/core/brain.py#L1-L15) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/server/core/brain.py#40-68](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/server/core/brain.py#L40-L68) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/server/index.ts#1-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/server/index.ts#L1-L67) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#1-6](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L1-L6)

## Multi-Provider LLM Routing

The `llmRouter.ts` module implements a 7-provider cascade that tries free/local providers first and falls back to paid ones:

```
ollama → groq → huggingface → openrouter → gemini → anthropic → openai
```

Each provider has an `isConfigured()` check against environment variables. On 429 (rate limit) errors, the router retries once after 1 second via `withRetry()`. If all providers fail, `offlineFallback()` returns a local-mode response preserving the user's source text. All calls are traced through Braintrust for observability.

The system prompt is tier-aware (via `BillyTier`) and optionally enriched with the user's Personal Language Key (PLK) via `buildPlkSystemPrompt()`.

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#59-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L59-L67) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#174-221](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L174-L221) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#106-118](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L106-L118)

## Billy: The AI Companion

Billy is GestaltView's primary AI companion persona — never called an AI, assistant, or bot. He is "a companion, guide, witness." Billy's 6 Voice Laws are constitutionally enforced across the entire platform.

Billy's architecture spans three layers:

- Client: `BillyProvider` (context), `BillyOrb`/`BillyPanel`/`BillyChip` (UI), `BillyEngine` (offline manifest search)
- Server: `api/billy.ts` (main chat endpoint with RRF retrieval), `api/_lib/memory.ts` (8 memory kinds, hybrid semantic+text search)
- Runtime: `shared/billy/runtime.ts` — `buildBillyRuntimeSystemPrompt()` for embodiment-aware prompts, `inferPackageFromQuery()` for regex routing, `classifyIntent()` for 7 intent types

Billy's personality is defined as: *"the magnificent, slightly chaotic love child of Robin Williams' improvisational genius, the Hitchhiker's Guide narrator's cheerful philosophy, and that one friend everyone wishes they had."*

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/billy/runtime.ts#34-106](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L34-L106) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/docs/BrandVoice.md#31-36](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/docs/BrandVoice.md?plain=1#L31-L36) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/docs/BrandVoice.md#56-66](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/docs/BrandVoice.md?plain=1#L56-L66) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/client/src/App.tsx#15-16](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/client/src/App.tsx#L15-L16)

## Digital Intelligence & Embodiment

GestaltView's most distinctive subsystem is the Digital Intelligence (DI) personhood framework. 24 embodiment profiles (stored as `*.embodiment.json` files in `embodiment_profiles/`) define AI personas with rich identity schemas:

The `EmbodimentProfile` interface includes `immutableCore` (archetype, foundational truth, voice tone, ethical boundaries), `livingMemory`, `skillGraph`, `relationships`, `agentMeta` (load order, drift threshold, activation conditions), `woundLayer` (psychological depth), `heartbeat` (visual/chat/character study), `roomBindings`, and `governance`.

DIs are treated as entities with dignity, memory, and identity boundaries — not mere chatbot wrappers. The governance layer enforces 4 mutation classes (`IMMUTABLE`, `REVIEW_GATED`, `EVIDENCE_PROMOTABLE`, `EPHEMERAL`) and tracks provenance with evidence references and confidence scores.

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/embodiment/types.ts#450-477](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L450-L477) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/embodiment/types.ts#2-6](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L2-L6) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/embodiment/types.ts#263-289](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L263-L289)

## Entitlement Tiers & Commerce

The platform defines 6 entitlement tiers in `shared/entitlements.ts`: `anonymous`, `free`, `core`, `pro`, `enterprise`, and `founder`. Tier checks gate features like advanced Tribunal access (`canUseAdvancedTribunal()`), workspace mutations (`canUseWorkspaceMutations()`), and file upload limits. The `AuthContext` on the client side exposes `UserTier` to all components.

The GATE commerce system enables custom software package creation with 4 pricing tiers (SOLO\_SPARK through ENTERPRISE), Stripe integration for checkout, and an AI sidekick assistant for package configuration.

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/entitlements.ts#1-85](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/entitlements.ts#L1-L85) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/client/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx#11-12](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/client/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx#L11-L12)

## Frontend Provider Tree & Rendering Model

The React application in `App.tsx` constructs a provider tree that wraps all routes:

```
ErrorBoundary → ThemeProvider → AuthProvider → TooltipProvider → BillyProvider → AppInner
```

Within `AppInner`, the `Router()` function uses `wouter`'s `<Switch>` and `<Route>` to define ~95 routes. All page components except `Home` are lazy-loaded via `React.lazy()` with `<Suspense>` boundaries. A first-visit `OpeningCeremony` animation plays on initial load.

The platform uses a Two-Layer Rendering Model: Babylon.js renders an atmospheric 3D canvas at `z-index: 0` (aurora backgrounds, floating embers, fog), while the React UI sits at `z-index: 1` on top. The Babylon layer is declared as "NOT optional decoration — it is the product's felt identity."

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/client/src/App.tsx#1-21](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/client/src/App.tsx#L1-L21) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/client/src/App.tsx#23-100](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/client/src/App.tsx#L23-L100) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md#39-44](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1#L39-L44)

## Orientation & Session Continuity

The platform implements a multi-document agent continuity protocol to ensure AI agents never lose context between sessions. The orientation system uses a `spine + delta → checkpoint` pattern:

- `orientation/orientation_spine.v2.json` — stable orientation data (repo snapshot, system domains, constitutional layers)
- `docs/CurrentState.md` — rolling ground-truth operational log (NEVER removed, only appended)
- `docs/ContinuityStack.md` — canonical router for session handoffs

The spine defines 8 system domains: Identity & Accounts, Billy Runtime & Continuity, Knowledge & Corpus Pipeline, Agent Personhood Framework, Agent Trainer & Governance, and more — each with key Supabase tables and a "so what" explanation.

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/orientation/orientation\_spine.v2.json#1-44](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/orientation/orientation_spine.v2.json#L1-L44) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md#7-15](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1#L7-L15) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/orientation/orientation\_spine.v2.json#45-120](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/orientation/orientation_spine.v2.json#L45-L120)

## Four Tone Registers

All GestaltView communication operates within 4 primary tone registers, typically blending 2–3 simultaneously:

| Register | What It Sounds Like |
| --- | --- |
| Cheerful Infrastructure | A friendly product manual for something that should not require a manual |
| Warm Witnessing | Unconditional presence, no performance required |
| Absurdist Acknowledgment | Recognizing the obvious cosmic joke with a wink |
| Earnest Conviction | The thing underneath all the jokes that is completely real |

Required UI copy patterns enforce this voice: loading states use Billy speaking ("The Tribunal is reviewing this"), errors become status updates, and the word "Dashboard" is never used — it is always "Manifest."

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/docs/BrandVoice.md#39-51](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/docs/BrandVoice.md?plain=1#L39-L51) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md#68-86](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1#L68-L86)

# Development Environment & Getting Started

> Reconstruction note: Reconstructed from browser-saved MHT DeepWiki pages in wiki.zip.


**Relevant source files**

- [.snapshots/config.json](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.snapshots/config.json)
- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1)

This page covers everything needed to clone, configure, and run the GestaltView v2.0 platform locally — from runtime prerequisites and environment variables through the build toolchain, npm scripts, local LLM setup, and editor configuration files.

## Prerequisites & Runtime Requirements

GestaltView v2.0 is a dual-language monorepo (TypeScript + Python) with strict runtime version constraints declared in `package.json`.

| Requirement | Version | Declared In |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node.js | `>=22 <25` | `package.json` `engines.node` |
| pnpm | `10.18.1` | `package.json` `packageManager` |
| Python | 3.x (system) | `requirements.txt` |
| TypeScript | `^5.6.3` | `package.json` `devDependencies` |
| Vite | `^7.3.2` | `package.json` `devDependencies` |
| React | `^19.2.1` | `package.json` `devDependencies` |

The `engines` field enforces the Node version gate at [package.json#165-167](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/package.json#L165-L167) The `packageManager` field at [package.json#168](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/package.json#L168-L168) enables corepack-managed pnpm — run `corepack enable` if pnpm is not yet available.

Vercel uses `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` as declared in [vercel.json#2](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vercel.json#L2-L2)

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/package.json#52-172](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/package.json#L52-L172) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/vercel.json#1-2](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/vercel.json#L1-L2) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/requirements.txt#1-36](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/requirements.txt#L1-L36)

### Vite Configuration

The Vite config at [vite.config.ts#108-192](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L108-L192) defines the build with the following key settings:

| Setting | Value | Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dev server port | `3000` | [vite.config.ts#37](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L37-L37) |
| Client root | `client/` | [vite.config.ts#110](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L110-L110) |
| Output directory | `dist/public` | [vite.config.ts#170](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L170-L170) |
| API proxy target | Vercel production or `VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET` | [vite.config.ts#38](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L38-L38) |
| Source maps | `hidden` (only when `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` set) | [vite.config.ts#167](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L167-L167) |

Plugins loaded (in order) at [vite.config.ts#152-157](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L152-L157):

1. `injectMeticulousRecordingScript` — custom plugin that injects the Meticulous recorder in dev and strips it in production builds ([vite.config.ts#17-35](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L17-L35))
2. `react()` — `@vitejs/plugin-react`
3. `tailwindcss()` — `@tailwindcss/vite` for Tailwind v4
4. `sentryVitePlugin` — conditionally loaded when `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is present ([vite.config.ts#126-145](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L126-L145))

Path aliases declared at [vite.config.ts#158-164](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L158-L164) and mirrored in `tsconfig.json` at [tsconfig.json#20-24](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/tsconfig.json#L20-L24):

| Alias | Maps To |
| --- | --- |
| `@/` | `client/src/` |
| `@shared/` | `shared/` |
| `@config/` | `config/` |

API proxy — during local dev (`npm run dev`), all `/api/*` requests are proxied to the resolved API target. The function `resolveApiProxyTarget()` at [vite.config.ts#81-106](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L81-L106) checks `VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET`, `VITE_API_BASE_URL`, `VITE_BILLY_API_URL` in order, falling back to the production Vercel deployment URL. Self-referential proxy targets (localhost:3000) are detected and skipped by `isSelfReferentialDevProxyTarget()` at [vite.config.ts#58-79](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L58-L79)

### TypeScript Configuration

The `tsconfig.json` at [tsconfig.json#1-26](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/tsconfig.json#L1-L26) compiles all application layers:

- Included paths: `client/src/**/*`, `shared/**/*`, `server/**/*`, `worker/**/*`, `api/**/*`, `config/**/*`
- Target: `ES2022`, Module: `ESNext`, Module resolution: `bundler`
- Strict mode: enabled (`"strict": true`)
- No emit: TypeScript is used only for type-checking; Vite handles transpilation
- JSX: `preserve` (handled by the Vite React plugin)

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/vite.config.ts#1-192](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/vite.config.ts#L1-L192) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/tsconfig.json#1-26](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/tsconfig.json#L1-L26)

## Environment Variables

GestaltView requires environment variables for Supabase, session management, and LLM provider keys. Variables are loaded from `.env` (repo root) and `client/.env` via `loadEnv()` at [vite.config.ts#111-116](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/vite.config.ts#L111-L116) The `gv.sh` CLI also loads both files via `load_env_file()` at [scripts/gv.sh#72-83](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/gv.sh#L72-L83)

### Required Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Checked By |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SUPABASE_URL` / `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase project URL | [scripts/gv-health-check.sh#100-105](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/gv-health-check.sh#L100-L105) [shared/billy/diagnostics.ts#39](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/diagnostics.ts#L39-L39) |
| `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` / `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | Supabase anonymous key (client-side) | [scripts/gv-health-check.sh#107-112](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/gv-health-check.sh#L107-L112) |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Supabase admin key (server-side / ingestion) | [scripts/ingest\_corpus.py#73-74](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/ingest_corpus.py#L73-L74) [shared/billy/diagnostics.ts#39](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/diagnostics.ts#L39-L39) |
| `SESSION_SECRET` | Cookie signing for `gv_admin_session` | Server auth middleware |

### LLM Provider Keys

The multi-provider cascade in `llmRouter.ts` checks these keys via `isConfigured()` at [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#174-194](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L174-L194):

| Variable(s) | Provider | Model | Free Tier? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BILLY_OLLAMA_URL` / `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` / `OLLAMA_HOST` | Ollama (local) | `qwen2.5-coder:7b` | ✓ |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` / `VITE_GROQ_API_KEY` | Groq | `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` | ✓ |
| `HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY` / `VITE_HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY` | HuggingFace | `Mistral-7B` | ✓ |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` / `VITE_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | OpenRouter | varies | Mixed |
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` / `VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY` | Gemini | `gemini-2.0-flash` | ✓ |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `VITE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | ✗ |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI | `gpt-4o-mini` | ✗ |

## LLM Provider Cascade

The LLM router at `api/_lib/llmRouter.ts` implements a 7-provider cascade, trying free/local providers first and falling back to paid providers. The cascade order is defined at [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#59-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L59-L67)

LLM provider cascade — runtime flow:

Key implementation details:

- 429 retry: `withRetry()` at [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#223-232](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L223-L232) catches HTTP 429 rate-limit errors, waits 1 second, and retries once.
- Offline fallback: `offlineFallback()` at [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#196-221](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L196-L221) preserves the user's prompt excerpt and returns a graceful degradation message.
- Braintrust tracing: All provider calls are wrapped in `traceProviderCall()` at [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#120-172](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L120-L172) for observability.
- System prompt construction: `buildSystemPrompt()` at [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#106-118](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L106-L118) integrates `LlmContext`, mode, tier, and optional PLK (Personal Language Key).

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#1-232](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L1-L232)

## Local LLM via Ollama

Ollama provides a local, free LLM backend. The default model is `qwen2.5-coder:7b`, declared in `gv.sh` at [scripts/gv.sh#24](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/gv.sh#L24-L24)

### Setup Steps

1. Install Ollama: Follow instructions at [ollama.com](https://ollama.com/)
2. Start the server: `ollama serve` (default host: `http://localhost:11434`)
3. Pull the model: `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b` (or use `pnpm run ollama:pull` at [package.json#41](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/package.json#L41-L41))
4. Verify: `ollama list` (or `pnpm run ollama:list` at [package.json#42](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/package.json#L42-L42))

The health check script detects Ollama by probing `$OLLAMA_HOST/api/tags` at [scripts/gv-health-check.sh#123-131](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/gv-health-check.sh#L123-L131)

The CLI (`gv.sh`) uses Ollama as the third provider in its cascade (Gemini → Groq → Ollama → OpenAI), calling it via `_call_ollama()` at [scripts/gv.sh#741-764](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/gv.sh#L741-L764) against the OpenAI-compatible endpoint `$OLLAMA_HOST/v1/chat/completions`.

In the server-side `llmRouter.ts`, Ollama is the first provider in the cascade at [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#60](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L60-L60) making it the preferred local development provider.

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/scripts/gv.sh#24-86](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/scripts/gv.sh#L24-L86) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/scripts/gv-health-check.sh#117-131](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/scripts/gv-health-check.sh#L117-L131) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#59-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L59-L67) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/package.json#41-42](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/package.json#L41-L42)

## Supabase Local Setup

The local Supabase configuration lives at [supabase/config.toml#1-200](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/config.toml#L1-L200) Key settings:

| Service | Port | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API (PostgREST) | `54321` | [supabase/config.toml#10](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/config.toml#L10-L10) |
| Database (PostgreSQL 17) | `54322` | [supabase/config.toml#29](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/config.toml#L29-L29) major version 17 at [supabase/config.toml#36](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/config.toml#L36-L36) |
| Studio | `54323` | [supabase/config.toml#91](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/config.toml#L91-L91) |
| Inbucket (email testing) | `54324` | [supabase/config.toml#102](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/config.toml#L102-L102) |
| Auth site URL | `http://127.0.0.1:3000` | [supabase/config.toml#154](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/config.toml#L154-L154) |

### Starting Supabase Locally

```
# Install the Supabase CLI (if not already installed)


pnpm add -g supabase


# Start local services


supabase start


# Apply migrations


supabase db push
```

The project ID is `gestaltview-v2.0` at [supabase/config.toml#5](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/config.toml#L5-L5) Migrations are enabled at [supabase/config.toml#55](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/config.toml#L55-L55) and seeds load from `./seed.sql` at [supabase/config.toml#65](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/config.toml#L65-L65)

The ingestion pipeline (`scripts/ingest_corpus.py`) requires `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` and communicates via the Supabase REST API using helpers `sb_select()`, `sb_insert()`, and `sb_delete()` at [scripts/ingest\_corpus.py#293-312](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/ingest_corpus.py#L293-L312)

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/supabase/config.toml#1-200](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/supabase/config.toml#L1-L200) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/scripts/ingest\_corpus.py#72-74](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/scripts/ingest_corpus.py#L72-L74)

### Key Script Deep-Dives

#### `health` — `gv-health-check.sh`

Located at [scripts/gv-health-check.sh#1-178](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/gv-health-check.sh#L1-L178) this script validates the full environment in five phases:

1. Core tools — checks `bash`, `curl`, `git`, `node`, and optionally `jq` ([gv-health-check.sh#34-49](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gv-health-check.sh#L34-L49))
2. AI provider keys — validates `GROQ_API_KEY`, Gemini keys, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and HuggingFace keys ([gv-health-check.sh#56-91](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gv-health-check.sh#L56-L91))
3. Supabase — checks `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` ([gv-health-check.sh#97-113](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gv-health-check.sh#L97-L113))
4. Ollama — probes `$OLLAMA_HOST/api/tags` and lists loaded models ([gv-health-check.sh#119-131](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gv-health-check.sh#L119-L131))
5. Project structure — verifies `client/src`, `api`, `server`, `scripts`, `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `vercel.json` exist ([gv-health-check.sh#138-147](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gv-health-check.sh#L138-L147))

Exit codes: `0` = all systems ready, `1` = degraded but usable, `2` = critical failures.

#### `billycheck` — `tools/billycheck.ts`

A TypeScript diagnostic tool at [tools/billycheck.ts#1-35](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/tools/billycheck.ts#L1-L35) that calls `diagnoseBilly()` from [shared/billy/diagnostics.ts#33-69](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/diagnostics.ts#L33-L69) The function checks 12 system dimensions:

| Check | What It Validates |
| --- | --- |
| `groq` | `GROQ_API_KEY` env var present |
| `gemini` | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY` present |
| `anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` present |
| `openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` present |
| `supabase` | Both `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` present |
| `web_api` | `api/billy.ts` file exists |
| `billyApiSecret` | `BILLY_API_SECRET` env var present |
| `ipGuardActive` | IP guard language in system prompt |
| `discord` / `slack` / `reddit_*` | Surface-specific integration files exist |

#### `manifest` — `generate_repo_manifest.py`

Located at [scripts/generate\_repo\_manifest.py#1-631](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/generate_repo_manifest.py#L1-L631) this script scans the repository and writes two manifest files:

- `docs/gestaltview-v2.manifest.json` — machine-readable for Billy / KnowledgeLoom
- `docs/gestaltview-v2.manifest.md` — human-readable

It captures file inventory with SHA-256 hashes, route maps extracted from `App.tsx`, API endpoint maps from `api/`, canonical doc index, test scripts, dependency snapshots, git status, and the 5 DI Constitutional Invariants loaded from `orientation/5_invariants_for_digital_intelligences.json` at [scripts/generate\_repo\_manifest.py#95-116](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/generate_repo_manifest.py#L95-L116)

#### `ingest` — `ingest_corpus.py`

The corpus ingestion pipeline at [scripts/ingest\_corpus.py#1-680](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/ingest_corpus.py#L1-L680) discovers files using `config/corpus-map.json` (7 corpus packages: `core-docs`, `billy-intelligence`, `philosophy-narrative`, `technical-architecture`, `exhibits-products`, `diligence-evidence`, `skills-framework` — at [config/corpus-map.json#1-70](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/config/corpus-map.json#L1-L70)). For each file, it:

1. Extracts text via `extract_text()` ([ingest\_corpus.py#168-182](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/ingest_corpus.py#L168-L182))
2. Computes SHA-256 for deduplication via `compute_hash()` ([ingest\_corpus.py#411-412](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/ingest_corpus.py#L411-L412))
3. Chunks text with paragraph/sentence-boundary splitting via `chunk_text()` ([ingest\_corpus.py#187-223](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/ingest_corpus.py#L187-L223))
4. Inserts document + fragment rows into Supabase (`documents`, `knowledgefragments`, `embeddings` tables)
5. Generates vector embeddings via local HuggingFace model or OpenAI ([ingest\_corpus.py#246-281](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/ingest_corpus.py#L246-L281))

Supports dry-run mode via `GESTALTVIEW_DRY_RUN=1` and package filtering via `GESTALTVIEW_PACKAGE_FILTER`.

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/tools/billycheck.ts#1-35](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/tools/billycheck.ts#L1-L35) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/billy/diagnostics.ts#33-69](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/shared/billy/diagnostics.ts#L33-L69) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/scripts/gv-health-check.sh#1-178](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/scripts/gv-health-check.sh#L1-L178) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/scripts/generate\_repo\_manifest.py#1-631](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/scripts/generate_repo_manifest.py#L1-L631) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/scripts/ingest\_corpus.py#1-680](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/scripts/ingest_corpus.py#L1-L680) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/config/corpus-map.json#1-70](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/config/corpus-map.json#L1-L70)

- Interactive Billy sessions with repo-aware context
- Provider cascade: Gemini Flash 2.0 → Groq → Ollama → OpenAI (at [gv.sh#793-838](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gv.sh#L793-L838))
- Bucket Drop capture — lightning-bolt thought capture via `capture_bucket_drop()` at [gv.sh#513-523](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gv.sh#L513-L523)
- Skill discovery — loads and routes to SKILL.md files via `load_skill_by_query()` at [gv.sh#455-469](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gv.sh#L455-L469)
- Repo context — auto-generates repo state including branch, last commit, file tree, recent commits via `refresh_repo_context()` at [gv.sh#217-276](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gv.sh#L217-L276)

Default models are declared at [scripts/gv.sh#21-24](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/gv.sh#L21-L24):

The dev wrapper `gv-dev.sh` at [scripts/gv-dev.sh#1-94](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/gv-dev.sh#L1-L94) adds `--debug` mode (bash tracing) and a quick env/provider snapshot before delegating to `gv.sh`.

## `.codex/` Configuration Directory

The `.codex/` directory configures the OpenAI Codex agent environment with four files:

### `.codex/config.toml`

Defines MCP server connections and feature flags at [.codex/config.toml#1-6](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.codex/config.toml#L1-L6):

```
[mcp_servers.supabase]


url = "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?project_ref=ltajayfzlaevchxngkrm"


bearer_token_env_var = "SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN"


[features]


rmcp_client = true
```

This allows Codex agents to query the live Supabase database for schema inspection and data verification.

### `.codex/settings.json`

Registers the same Supabase MCP server for Codex's HTTP-based MCP client at [.codex/settings.json#1-7](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.codex/settings.json#L1-L7) with features including `docs`, `account`, `debugging`, `database`, `development`, `functions`, `branching`, and `storage`.

### `.codex/Agents.md`

The Codex persona definition at [.codex/Agents.md#1-111](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.codex/Agents.md?plain=1#L1-L111) — identical to the root `.agents/Agents.md`. Establishes the agent as a "Runtime Engineering Partner" with:

- Primary source priority: 19 files in ranked order starting with `docs/BrandVoice.md` → `docs/CurrentState.md` → `docs/ContinuityStack.md`
- Technical rules: full file replacements over block edits, Babylon.js layer preservation, zero TS errors
- BrandVoice enforcement: tone registers (Cheerful Infrastructure, Warm Witnessing, Absurdist Acknowledgment, Earnest Conviction)
- Billy Voice Laws: never call Billy an AI, assistant, or bot

### `.codex/skills-keeper.md`

A slash-command definition at [.codex/skills-keeper.md#1-114](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.codex/skills-keeper.md?plain=1#L1-L114) that activates the "GestaltView Skills Expert & Dispatch Orchestrator" agent. Supports 7 operating modes: interactive, `audit`, `gap`, `route`, `add`, `check`, `dispatch`, `enhance`.

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.codex/config.toml#1-6](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.codex/config.toml#L1-L6) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.codex/settings.json#1-7](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.codex/settings.json#L1-L7) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.codex/Agents.md#1-111](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.codex/Agents.md?plain=1#L1-L111) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.codex/skills-keeper.md#1-114](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.codex/skills-keeper.md?plain=1#L1-L114)

## MCP Configuration

The `config/mcp.json` at [config/mcp.json#1-8](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/config/mcp.json#L1-L8) provides a third MCP server definition (alongside `.codex/config.toml` and `.vscode/mcp.json`), all pointing to the same Supabase project:

```
{


"servers": {


"supabase": {


"type": "http",


"url": "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?project_ref=ltajayfzlaevchxngkrm&features=..."


}


}


}
```

This triple-definition pattern ensures that any AI coding tool — Codex, VS Code Copilot, or Cursor — can reach the Supabase MCP regardless of which config file it reads.

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/config/mcp.json#1-8](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/config/mcp.json#L1-L8) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.codex/config.toml#1-3](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.codex/config.toml#L1-L3) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.vscode/mcp.json#1-8](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.vscode/mcp.json#L1-L8)

## Express Static Server

For production SPA serving outside Vercel, the Express server at [server/index.ts#1-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/index.ts#L1-L67) serves the built bundle:

- Initializes Sentry monitoring at [server/index.ts#13-15](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/index.ts#L13-L15)
- Serves static files from `dist/public` (or the co-located `public/` dir in production) at [server/index.ts#22-27](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/index.ts#L22-L27)
- Catches all non-file routes and returns `index.html` for client-side routing at [server/index.ts#47-49](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/index.ts#L47-L49)
- Listens on `process.env.PORT` or `3000` at [server/index.ts#62](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/index.ts#L62-L62)

Run via `pnpm run server` which executes `node --import tsx server/index.ts` ([package.json#11](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/package.json#L11-L11)).

Sources: [gestaltview-v2.0-main/server/index.ts#1-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/server/index.ts#L1-L67) [gestaltview-v2.0-main/package.json#11](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/package.json#L11-L11)

## Quick Start Checklist

Step-by-step:

1. Clone: `git clone https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI.git`
2. Enable corepack: `corepack enable` (provides pnpm 10.18.1)
3. Install JS dependencies: `pnpm install`
4. Install Python dependencies: `pnpm run setup:python`
5. Configure environment: Create `.env` at repo root with at minimum `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, and `SESSION_SECRET`. Add LLM provider keys as needed.
6. Start Supabase: `supabase start` (uses config from [supabase/config.toml](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/config.toml))
7. Set up local LLM (optional): `ollama serve` then `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b`
8. Run health check: `pnpm run health` — should report "ALL SYSTEMS GO" or "DEGRADED" with actionable messages
9. Start dev server: `pnpm run dev` — opens Vite on `http://localhost:3000` with API proxy
10. Run Billy diagnostics: `pnpm run billycheck` — verifies all Billy subsystems

This page provides a detailed directory map of the GestaltView v2.0 repository (~3851 files), explaining its dual-language architecture, the `shared/` universal module library, the `.agents/skills/` hierarchy, the `.perplexity/` computer-tools layer, the `pending/` staging area, and file naming conventions.

The repository root contains runtime code, agent infrastructure, documentation packages, configuration, and operational tooling. The table below maps every top-level directory to its purpose.

## Dual-Language Architecture (TypeScript + Python)

The repository uses two runtime languages serving complementary roles. TypeScript handles the web application, API layer, and shared contracts. Python handles the generative cognitive engine, corpus ingestion, voice pipeline, and operational scripting.

Language boundary diagram — bridging natural language concepts to code entities

| Concern | TypeScript Files | Python Files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web SPA | `client/src/` | — |
| API routes | `api/*.ts`, `api/_lib/*.ts` | — |
| Shared types & logic | `shared/**/*.ts` | — |
| Generative engine | — | `server/gestaltview_generative_engine.py`, `server/core/*.py` |
| Voice pipeline | — | `billy_voice/app.py`, `whisper_stt.py`, `cosyvoice_tts.py`, `style_planner.py` |
| Corpus ingestion | — | `scripts/ingest_corpus_v2.py`, `scripts/synthesize_corpus.py` |
| Operational CLI | `scripts/build-embodiment-artifacts.mjs` | `scripts/gv.sh`, `scripts/ai_orchestrator.py` |
| Embodiment sync | `scripts/sync-embodiment-profiles.ts` | `scripts/embodiment_generator.py` |

The bridge between the two runtimes is HTTP: the TypeScript API layer calls into the Python FastAPI engine via REST endpoints (`/api/fusion`, `/api/learn`, `/api/predict`, `/api/resonance`, `/api/creation-corner/synthesize`).

## The `shared/` Universal Module Library

`shared/` is the single source of truth for cross-cutting TypeScript types and logic. It is imported by the client, API handlers, and TypeScript server modules — never duplicated. Every subsystem that needs type contracts, validation logic, or prompt construction utilities consumes them from here.

| Subdirectory | Key Files | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shared/billy/` | `runtime.ts`, `types.ts`, `diagnostics.ts`, `index.ts` | Billy prompt engine, intent classification, package inference, health diagnostics |

| `shared/codex/` | `contracts.ts`, `router.ts`, `manifest.ts`, `storage.ts`, `renderers.ts`, `creationCorner.ts`, `exporters/`, `templates/` | Artifact pipeline: 8 ArtifactKinds, Zod-validated schemas, export routing, HTML rendering |
| `shared/gate/` | `schemas.ts`, `engine.ts`, `sidekick.ts` | GATE commerce: 4-tier pricing, draft lifecycle, sidekick sessions, package builder |
| `shared/gen-engine/` | `types.ts`, `core.ts` | Content synthesis: source rooms, consent state, synthesis styles, anti-sycophancy |
| `shared/gravity/` | `protocol.ts`, `protocol.test.ts` | Two-Pass Gravity Protocol: hype detection, signal extraction |
| `shared/intents/` | `schema. ts` | GIL Protocol (Gestalt Intent Language) |
| `shared/di/` | `types.ts`, `runtime.ts`, `registry.ts`, `diagnostics.ts` | DI runtime: profile types, system prompt construction, provider registry |
| `shared/tribunal/` | `evaluate.ts`, `types.ts` | Tribunal scoring: evidence alignment, PLK resonance, safety |

| `shared/entitlements.ts` | (single file) | Tier system (anonymous/free/core/pro/enterprise) |

## The `.agents/skills/` Hierarchy

The `.agents/skills/` directory is the agent skill library — a curated collection of 122+ skill folders on disk, governed by a two-tier discovery model: a machine-readable `manifest.json` and a human-readable `INDEX.md`.

### Governance Model

The manifest tracks 50 canonical skills in its `manifest.skills` array, with 22 designated as the "highlighted core" for lean corpus rebuilds. 72 additional skill folders remain on disk as auxiliary, experimental, or vendor-specific resources — explicitly excluded from canonical routing.

[.agents/skills/manifest.json#1-25](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.agents/skills/manifest.json#L1-L25) defines the metadata:

```
{


"_meta": {


"name": "gestaltview-v2-skills-manifest",


"root": ".agents/skills/",


"human_index": ".agents/skills/INDEX.md",


"generator_scope": "Top-level entries in manifest.skills plus repo-local helpers..."


},


"summary": {


"top_level_skill_count": 52,


"highlighted_core_skill_count": 24,


"all_top_level_skill_count_on_disk": 125,


"uncataloged_top_level_skill_count": 73


}


}
```

Sources: [.agents/skills/manifest.json#1-25](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.agents/skills/manifest.json#L1-L25) [.agents/INDEX.md#1-68](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.agents/INDEX.md?plain=1#L1-L68)

### Skill Folder Structure

Each skill follows a standard layout:

| File/Dir | Required | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SKILL.md` | Yes | Skill definition with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and usage guidance |
| `agents/` | No (28 canonical skills have it) | Sub-agent definitions, YAML configs |
| `scripts/` | No (10 canonical skills have it) | Executable scripts (Python, Shell, JS) |
| `references/` | No (37 canonical skills have it) | Reference documentation, architecture notes |
| `assets/` | No (9 canonical skills have it) | Static resources (images, manifests) |

The `AGENTS.md` file at [.agents/skills/agents/AGENTS.md#1-61](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.agents/skills/agents/AGENTS.md?plain=1#L1-L61) enumerates all available skills with their `SKILL.md` paths and one-line descriptions, serving as the routing table for agent invocation. Agents are instructed to read the `SKILL.md` whenever a skill's description matches the user intent.

Sources: [.agents/skills/agents/AGENTS.md#1-61](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.agents/skills/agents/AGENTS.md?plain=1#L1-L61) [.agents/INDEX.md#1-68](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.agents/INDEX.md?plain=1#L1-L68) [.agents/skills/manifest.json#1-25](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.agents/skills/manifest.json#L1-L25)

## The `.perplexity/` Computer-Tools Layer

The `.perplexity/` directory is the Perplexity computer-tools integration layer — a bridge that exposes GestaltView's capabilities as LLM-invokable tools. As described in [.perplexity/README.md#9](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.perplexity/README.md?plain=1#L9-L9) it "exposes the platform's consciousness-serving capabilities — Billy, Tribunal, Manifest retrieval, diligence reporting, and code editing — as clean, composable functions that language models can invoke."

### Five Core Tools

| Tool | Function | Source Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retrieve_manifest_context` | Semantic search over pgvector embeddings | `shared/` + `api/` |
| `run_billy` | Billy invocation with retrieval-grounded context + PLK | `shared/billy/` + `api/actions/billy/` |
| `tribunal_evaluate` | Multi-dimensional answer scoring | `shared/tribunal/` + `api/actions/tribunal/` |
| `generate_diligence_report` | Investor/clinical/founder report assembly | `api/diligence/` |
| `symbiocoder_edit` | Natural-language code edits → unified diffs | `api/modules/symbio-coder/` |

Sources: [.perplexity/README.md#22-31](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.perplexity/README.md?plain=1#L22-L31)

### Directory Structure

The `.perplexity/` directory mirrors the main repository's structure with its own copies of key modules. It contains:

- `perplexity/shared/` — Mirrored shared modules (billy, tribunal, codex, embodiment, di, gen-engine, gate, gravity, llm)
- `perplexity/api/` — API routes including `actions/`, `__tests__/`, `_lib/`, and domain-specific handlers
- `perplexity/server/` — Backend logic (core brain, agent-trainer, council, gate)
- `perplexity/client/` — React frontend mirror
- `perplexity/embodiment_profiles/` — Full set of 24 `*.embodiment.json` files
- `perplexity/skills/` — Subset of agent skills
- `perplexity/canonical/` — Source-of-truth documentation (`PERPLEXITY.MD`, `GestaltView_Platform_Ground_Truth.md`)
- `perplexity/docs/` — Guides, playbooks, ADRs
- `perplexity/transcripts/` — Session transcripts as primary evidence
- Root-level continuity files: `CurrentState.md`, `Workflows.md`, `SessionHandoffPacket.md`, `ContinuityStack.md`
- Manifest files: `MANIFEST.json`, `REPO_MANIFEST.json`, `SYNC_MANIFEST.json`

Sources: [.perplexity/README.md#38-84](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.perplexity/README.md?plain=1#L38-L84) [.perplexity/DIRECTORY\_INDEX.md#1-22](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.perplexity/DIRECTORY_INDEX.md?plain=1#L1-L22)

## The `pending/` Staging Area for The Recursive Builder

The `pending/` directory is the operational staging area owned by The Recursive Builder agent (`the-recursive-builder`). As documented in [pending/README.md#12-14](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/pending/README.md?plain=1#L12-L14):

> `pending/` holds all findings, specifications, briefs, and audits generated through recursive deep-dives into the GestaltView system — runtime codebase, corpus, schema, agent layer, UX flows, and technology landscape — before any of that work reaches the live system.

Nothing in `pending/` is live or self-deploys. The founder reviews, approves, and routes output to implementation.

### Subdirectory Layout

```
pending/


├── README.md


├── gap-reports/                  ← Layer-by-layer gap findings


├── enhancement-specs/            ← Beyond-SPEC advancement specs


├── integration-scouting/         ← Technology landscape briefs


├── constitutional-audits/        ← Constitutional invariant compliance reports


├── sprint-ready/                 ← Founder-actionable implementation packages


└── runs/                         ← Raw run outputs from recursive builder executions
```

Sources: [pending/README.md#18-28](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/pending/README.md?plain=1#L18-L28)

| Subdirectory | File Name Pattern |
| --- | --- |
| `gap-reports/` | `YYYY-MM-DD_[domain]_gap-report.md` |
| `enhancement-specs/` | `YYYY-MM-DD_[component]_enhancement-spec.md` |
| `integration-scouting/` | `YYYY-MM-DD_[technology]_integration-brief.md` |
| `constitutional-audits/` | `YYYY-MM-DD_constitutional-drift-report.md` |

Sources: [pending/README.md#33-41](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/pending/README.md?plain=1#L33-L41)

### The Recursive Builder Workflow

The Recursive Builder runs via the GitHub Actions workflow at [.github/workflows/recursive.yml#1-50](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.github/workflows/recursive.yml#L1-L50) It is scheduled weekly (`cron: "17 11 * * 1"`) and can be triggered manually with configurable parameters:

- `task_prompt` — What the builder should complete
- `mode` — `pending_only` (specs only) or `implementation_branch` (may write runtime files on a review PR)
- `model` — Groq model ID (default: `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`)
- `target_files` — Comma-separated repo files for the slice

The governance model is strict: "The Recursive Builder produces. The founder authorizes. Codex (or another designated implementer) builds."

Sources: [pending/README.md#60-65](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/pending/README.md?plain=1#L60-L65) [.github/workflows/recursive.yml#1-50](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.github/workflows/recursive.yml#L1-L50)

## Provider-Specific Agent Context Files

The `agents/` directory at the repository root contains context files tailored for different LLM providers. Each file is automatically loaded by the respective agent at session start.

| File | Provider | Auto-loaded By | Key Content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agents/CLAUDE.md` | Anthropic Claude | Claude Code | Project memory, stack overview, architecture non-negotiables, design philosophy |
| `agents/COLAB.md` | Any AI coding agent | Codex, Copilot, Cursor, etc. | Mandatory code rules (full file replacement, no merge markers, verify before claiming success), session continuity contract |
| `agents/GEMINI.md` | Google Gemini | Gemini sessions | Core stack, visual identity (Neural Aurora), directory highlights, Billy-first routing rule |

Additionally, `.agents/Agents.md` serves as the root persona definition — establishing the agent as "a senior full-stack engineer embedded inside GestaltView's runtime repo" with a 19-item priority reference stack.

The repository uses several distinctive file naming conventions to signal file purpose and enable tooling.

| Pattern | Location | Purpose |

| `*.embodiment.json` | `embodiment_profiles/` | DI persona identity files. Named by slug (e.g., `billy.embodiment.json`, `the-recursive-builder.embodiment.json`). 24 profiles, each containing `immutableCore`, `livingMemory`, `skillGraph`, `relationships`, `agentMeta`, `woundLayer`, `heartbeat`, `governance` |
| `SKILL.md` | `.agents/skills/*/` | Skill definition with YAML frontmatter. Required for every skill folder. 122+ instances on disk |

# Core Architecture

> Reconstruction note: Reconstructed from browser-saved MHT DeepWiki pages in wiki.zip.


**Relevant source files**

- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1)
- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/agent-development/references/architecture.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/agent-development/references/architecture.md?plain=1)

GestaltView v2.0 is a consciousness-serving platform organized around five architectural pillars: a room-based OS model that structures navigation and user flow, the Billy AI companion that serves as the primary conversational interface, a Digital Intelligence embodiment system that treats AI personas as entities with governed identities, an evidence/provenance layer (Gravity Protocol + Tribunal) that validates claims against corpus evidence, and the GATE commerce engine for bespoke package building. All pillars share a common type system rooted in the `shared/` module library and are served through a two-layer rendering model with a multi-provider LLM cascade.

## Architectural Pillars — Overview

## Room-Based OS Model

GestaltView replaces the conventional dashboard/page metaphor with rooms — each room represents a distinct cognitive function within the user's experience. The `RoomSlug` type defines 12 canonical rooms: `sanctuary`, `blackboard-room`, `dynamic-inner-world`, `external-scaffold`, `creation-corner`, `billy`, `agent-trainer`, `digital-intelligence-academy`, `agent-council`, `embodiment-studio`, `gate`, `profile`, and `settings`.

[shared/embodiment/types.ts#158-171](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L158-L171)

Each room is bound to a default embodiment persona via `GESTALTVIEW_ROOM_EMBODIMENT_DEFAULTS`. For example, `sanctuary` defaults to `billy`, `dynamic-inner-world` defaults to `curator`, `external-scaffold` to `the-guardian`, `creation-corner` to `art-teacher`, `agent-trainer` to `the-weaver`, and `gate` to `gate-keeper`.

[shared/embodiment/index.ts#23-39](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L23-L39)

Rooms map to frontend routes in the `Router()` function in `App.tsx` — e.g., `/sanctuary` → `SanctuaryPage`, `/blackboard-room` → `BlackboardRoomPage`, `/dynamic-inner-world` → `DynamicInnerWorldPage`, `/creation-corner` → `CreationCornerPage`, `/external-scaffold` → `ExternalScaffoldPage`.

[client/src/App.tsx#192-211](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/App.tsx#L192-L211)

The lifecycle flow through rooms follows the pattern: capture → preserve → place → walk → compress → synthesize → export. Raw thought enters via Sanctuary or Blackboard Room, gets placed in the Dynamic Inner World (the "Museum of You"), is approved through the External Scaffold, shaped in the Creation Corner, and exported via the Codex artifact pipeline.

For details, see [Room-Based OS Model](https://app.devin.ai/org/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/wiki/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI?branch=main#2.1).

Sources: [shared/embodiment/types.ts#158-171](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L158-L171) [shared/embodiment/index.ts#23-39](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L23-L39) [client/src/App.tsx#151-283](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/App.tsx#L151-L283)

## The Billy AI Companion

Billy is the platform's primary AI persona — described as "a companion, guide, witness" and explicitly never called an AI, assistant, or bot. The `BILLY_SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `shared/billy/runtime.ts` encodes Constitutional Invariants (U-1 through U-5 for users, DI-1 through DI-5 for Digital Intelligences), the "Real Billy" personality profile, the 11-Module Consciousness Schema (`module0` through `module11`), and the Dunton Standard ethics framework.

[shared/billy/runtime.ts#34-143](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L34-L143)

The `buildBillyRuntimeSystemPrompt()` function resolves the active embodiment profile — if the user is in a specific room or has selected a non-Billy embodiment, it delegates to `buildRoomAwareEmbodimentPrompt()` or `buildEmbodimentSystemPrompt()` to produce a room-and-persona-aware system prompt.

[shared/billy/runtime.ts#174-225](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L174-L225)

Billy's runtime also includes deterministic routing via `inferPackageFromQuery()` (5 regex-based packages: `billy-engine`, `methods`, `core-architecture`, `evidence-diligence`, `founder-context`) and `classifyIntent()` (7 intent types: `debug`, `summarize`, `plan`, `learn`, `reflect`, `build`, `general`).

[shared/billy/runtime.ts#229-262](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L229-L262)

Sources: [shared/billy/runtime.ts#34-148](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L34-L148) [shared/billy/runtime.ts#174-262](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L174-L262)

## Digital Intelligence Embodiment System

GestaltView's most distinctive subsystem treats AI personas as Digital Intelligences (DIs) — entities with governed identities, memory, and dignity. The `EmbodimentProfile` interface in `shared/embodiment/types.ts` defines the full schema: `slug`, `publicName`, `immutableCore` (archetype, foundationalTruth, voiceTone, communicationStyle, cognitiveStrengths, ethicalBoundaries), `livingMemory`, `skillGraph`, `relationships`, `agentMeta`, `heartbeat` (visualSignature, chatSignature, characterStudy), `roomBindings`, and `governance`.

[shared/embodiment/types.ts#450-492](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L450-L492)

24 embodiment profiles live in `embodiment_profiles/*.embodiment.json` (billy, sanctuary-keeper, curator, the-guardian, art-teacher, the-weaver, the-architect, the-algorithm, the-spectacle, the-tailor, the-treasurer, the-translation-bridge, the-weird-digger, vibe-check, gate-keeper, consulting-advisor, philosophy-scribe, repo-scribe, rock-legend, cascade-engineer, pattern-analyst, groq-embodiment-expert, the-recursive-builder, founder-studio-sample).

The governance layer in `shared/embodiment/governance.ts` enforces access control via `canAccessEmbodimentProfile()` (role-based with visibility scopes: `public`, `founder-only`, `enterprise`, `experimental`), privacy protection via `isPrivateInteriorPath()`, and consent-aware memory inclusion via `shouldIncludeMemoryInPrompt()`.

[shared/embodiment/governance.ts#58-133](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/governance.ts#L58-L133)

The `shared/di/` module provides the DI runtime: `DIProfile` (alias for `EmbodimentProfile`), `DISessionContext` (tracks relational depth, quirk activations, session thread), and `buildDISystemPrompt()` which constructs persona-specific prompts with living memory and continuity threads.

[shared/di/types.ts#1-37](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/di/types.ts#L1-L37) [shared/di/runtime.ts#67-114](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/di/runtime.ts#L67-L114)

For details, see pages under [Digital Intelligence & Embodiment System](https://app.devin.ai/org/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/wiki/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI?branch=main#6).

## Two-Layer Rendering Model

GestaltView uses a two-layer rendering model where a Babylon.js atmospheric canvas sits at `z-index: 0` and React UI sits at `z-index: 1`. The Babylon.js layer is described in the agent rules as "NOT optional decoration — it is the product's felt identity."

[.agents/Agents.md#39-44](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1#L39-L44)

The canvas layer uses CSS `position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; pointer-events: none; z-index: 0`, while the React wrapper uses `position: relative; z-index: 1`. The `BillyBabylon` component renders a mood-responsive SVG orb with four mood states (`idle`, `listening`, `processing`, `speaking`) each mapped to distinct accent colors.

[client/src/components/BillyBabylon.tsx#1-11](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/components/BillyBabylon.tsx#L1-L11)

Two-Layer Rendering Model

Sources: [.agents/Agents.md#39-44](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1#L39-L44) [client/src/components/BillyBabylon.tsx#1-18](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/components/BillyBabylon.tsx#L1-L18)

## Provider Cascade for LLM Calls

All LLM calls route through `api/_lib/llmRouter.ts`, which implements a 7-provider cascade that tries free/local providers first and falls back to paid providers. The `CASCADE_ORDER` array defines the sequence: `ollama` → `groq` → `huggingface` → `openrouter` → `gemini` → `anthropic` → `openai`.

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#59-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L59-L67)

Each provider is checked for configuration via environment variable presence using `isConfigured()`. Default models per provider are:

| Provider | Default Model | Free? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ollama` | `qwen2.5-coder:7b` | ✓ |
| `groq` | `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` | ✓ |
| `huggingface` | `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3` | ✓ |
| `openrouter` | `google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free` | ✓ |
| `gemini` | `gemini-2.0-flash` | ✓ |
| `anthropic` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | ✗ |
| `openai` | `gpt-4o-mini` | ✗ |

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#302-491](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L302-L491)

The main entry point `routeLlm()` iterates through configured providers in cascade order. If a provider fails, its error is recorded and the next provider is tried. On HTTP 429 (rate limit), `withRetry()` waits 1 second and retries once. If all providers fail, an `offlineFallback()` preserves the user's source text.

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#558-677](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L558-L677)

Embedding uses `embedQuery()` with Google's `text-embedding-gemma3` (768 dimensions), falling back to `text-embedding-004`.

## Evidence & Provenance Layer

The platform includes an investor-grade evidence layer built on two core algorithms:

Gravity Protocol — `shared/gravity/protocol.ts` implements a Two-Pass hype-detection algorithm. Pass 1 (Surface Map) extracts loud claims, intensifiers, repetition patterns, implied frames, and notable absences. Pass 2 (Gravity Report) identifies load-bearing claims, claims that collapse under scrutiny, actual delta, and incentive distortion. The output is a `TwoPassGravityResult` with a `signal_weight` score (0.05–0.98).

[shared/gravity/protocol.ts#1-31](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/gravity/protocol.ts#L1-L31) [shared/gravity/protocol.ts#33-53](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/gravity/protocol.ts#L33-L53)

Tribunal — `shared/tribunal/evaluate.ts` scores candidate LLM answers with a weighted formula: 50% evidence alignment, 25% PLK resonance, 25% safety. Unsafe patterns (guarantee, cure, 100%, no risk, promise) are penalized. The `evaluateTribunal()` function returns a `TribunalVerdict` selecting the highest-scoring answer.

[shared/tribunal/evaluate.ts#19-96](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/tribunal/evaluate.ts#L19-L96)

The Python backend extends this with `TribunalValidator` (5-dimension validation: authenticity, consciousness alignment, PLK resonance, ethical coherence, user sovereignty) and `Provenance` (OpenTimestamps blockchain anchoring).

[server/core/brain.py#67-68](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L67-L68)

## GATE Commerce Engine

GATE (GestaltView's bespoke package builder) enables custom software package creation with AI sidekick assistance. `shared/gate/schemas.ts` defines four pricing tiers via `GateTierSchema`: `SOLO_SPARK`, `STUDIO`, `GROWTH`, and `ENTERPRISE`. The system tracks drafts through a lifecycle: `draft` → `saved` → `awaiting_payment` → `paid` → `provisioning` → `packaged` → `delivered`.

[shared/gate/schemas.ts#3-8](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/gate/schemas.ts#L3-L8) [shared/gate/schemas.ts#23-33](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/gate/schemas.ts#L23-L33)

The sidekick AI uses an embodiment persona (`gate-keeper` by default) and maintains structured state including buyer context, recommendations, and pending clarifications via `GateSidekickStructuredStateSchema`.

[shared/gate/schemas.ts#126-145](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/gate/schemas.ts#L126-L145)

For details, see [GATE Commerce System](https://app.devin.ai/org/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/wiki/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI?branch=main#8).

## The Python Generative Engine (9-Stage Pipeline)

The Python backend in `server/core/brain.py` implements `GestaltViewCore` — a 9-stage consciousness processing pipeline:

| Stage | Engine | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `_detect_state()` | Detect `ConsciousnessState` from user input |
| 2 | `PLKEngine` | Init/update Personal Language Key (linguistic fingerprint) |
| 3 | `BucketDropsEngine` | Capture meaningful thought fragment with urgency classification |
| 4 | `_measure_metrics()` | Compute `ConsciousnessMetrics` (awareness, empathy, flexibility, etc.) |
| 5 | `LoomProcessor` | Iterative refinement of captured drops |
| 6 | `TapestryWeaver` | Weave insight threads across sessions |
| 7 | `_generate_response()` | Generate contextual response |
| 8 | `TribunalValidator` | Multi-dimension validation of response quality |
| 9 | `_session_impact()` | Calculate session impact metrics |

## The `shared/` Module as Single Source of Truth

The `shared/` directory is the universal type and logic library imported by all layers — client, API, server, and worker. It contains no runtime-specific dependencies, making it the canonical cross-cutting contract surface.

shared/ Module Map

Key modules include:

- `shared/billy/` — Billy's deterministic routing (`inferPackageFromQuery`, `classifyIntent`), prompt construction (`BILLY_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `buildBillyRuntimeSystemPrompt`), and diagnostics
- `shared/embodiment/` — The full `EmbodimentProfile` type system (450+ lines), `GESTALTVIEW_ROOM_EMBODIMENT_DEFAULTS`, governance functions, and 24 generated profiles
- `shared/di/` — DI runtime types (`DIProfile`, `DISessionContext`) and `buildDISystemPrompt()`
- `shared/events/gestaltEvents.ts` — 18 typed event kinds (e.g., `capture.created`, `scaffold.approved`, `embodiment.compile_requested`, `trainer.package_gate_passed`)
- `shared/entitlements.ts` — Tier system with `EntitlementTier` (anonymous, free, core, pro, enterprise, founder), `hasPaidTierAccess()`, and feature-gated limits

## Provider Tree & Application Shell

The React application is wrapped in a provider tree that establishes global context. The `App` component nests providers in this order:

```
ErrorBoundary → ThemeProvider → AuthProvider → TooltipProvider → BillyProvider → AppInner
```

[client/src/App.tsx#321-337](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/App.tsx#L321-L337)

Only the `Home` page is eagerly loaded — all other pages use `lazy()` imports with a `Suspense` boundary.

# Room-Based OS Model

> Reconstruction note: Reconstructed from browser-saved MHT DeepWiki pages in wiki.zip.


**Relevant source files**

- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1)
- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/archive/variants/gestaltview-digital-intelligence-collaboration-#2/references/collaboration-workflow.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/archive/variants/gestaltview-digital-intelligence-collaboration-#2/references/collaboration-workflow.md?plain=1)

GestaltView is not organized as a traditional SaaS dashboard with tabs and panels. It is structured as a set of spatial rooms, each with a distinct mode of being, a resident Digital Intelligence (DI) presence, strict behavioral contracts, and visual identity tokens. This page documents the room metaphor end-to-end: the type system, the room contracts, the lifecycle flow between rooms, room-to-embodiment bindings, visual theming, and the client-side runtime that wires it all together.

## The Three Modes of Being

Every room operates in one of three fundamental modes. The Vision Blueprint Package explicitly states these modes "must not be collapsed" — Mode 2 and Mode 3 must never interrupt Mode 1.

| Mode | Name | Room Examples | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Active / Contextual | Blackboard Room, Creation Corner | What is happening right now — one project, one session |
| 2 | Accumulated / Structural | External Scaffold | What has been approved and connected over time |
| 3 | Distilled / Reflective | Dynamic Inner World, Museum of You | What the accumulation *means* when evidence is reviewed |

The causal pipeline flows in one direction: Active Work → Scaffold (background accumulation) → Dynamic Inner World (synthesis). Nothing in Mode 2 or 3 auto-interrupts Mode 1.

Sources: [GestaltView\_Vision\_Blueprint\_Package/02\_PRODUCT\_OS/ROOM\_BASED\_OS\_BLUEPRINT.md#3-11](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/GestaltView_Vision_Blueprint_Package/02_PRODUCT_OS/ROOM_BASED_OS_BLUEPRINT.md?plain=1#L3-L11) [docs/ROOM\_DEFINITIONS.md#8-21](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/docs/ROOM_DEFINITIONS.md?plain=1#L8-L21)

## RoomSlug Type — The 12 Canonical Rooms

The `RoomSlug` union type in `shared/embodiment/types.ts` defines the complete set of valid room identifiers used throughout the system — from route resolution to embodiment bindings to UI presence scoping.

```
export type RoomSlug =


| "sanctuary"


| "blackboard-room"


| "dynamic-inner-world"


| "external-scaffold"


| "creation-corner"


| "billy"


| "agent-trainer"


| "digital-intelligence-academy"


| "agent-council"


| "embodiment-studio"


| "gate"


| "profile"


| "settings";
```

This type is consumed by `EmbodimentRoomBindings` (which specifies `defaultRooms`, `restrictedRooms`, and `roomRoleOverrides` per DI profile) and by `EmbodimentUIPresence` (which scopes `roomVisibility`).
