# Vercel Serverless API Layer

> Reconstruction note: Reconstructed from browser-saved MHT DeepWiki pages in wiki.zip.


**Relevant source files**

- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/agent-development/references/api-reference.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/agent-development/references/api-reference.md?plain=1)
- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/chatgpt-apps/actions/fastapi\_actions\_stub.py](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/chatgpt-apps/actions/fastapi_actions_stub.py)
- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/chatgpt-apps/actions/gestaltview\_gpt\_actions\_core.openapi.yaml](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/chatgpt-apps/actions/gestaltview_gpt_actions_core.openapi.yaml)

This page provides a deep dive into the `api/` directory — approximately 245 TypeScript files that form GestaltView's serverless backend, deployed as individual Vercel functions. Every route follows a composable-helpers pattern: shared `_lib/` utilities for auth, CORS, rate limiting, response envelopes, and Sentry wrapping are composed inside each handler rather than relying on a central middleware stack.

## Architecture Overview

Request Lifecycle — Natural Language to Code Entities

Sources: [api/billy.ts#1-14](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L1-L14) [api/\_lib/auth.ts#368-458](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/auth.ts#L368-L458) [api/\_lib/cors.ts#73-85](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/cors.ts#L73-L85) [api/\_lib/response.ts#19-61](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/response.ts#L19-L61) [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#1-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L1-L67)

## `_lib/` Shared Library

The `api/_lib/` directory contains ~20 modules that every route imports from. These are composable helper functions, not Express-style middleware.

### `auth.ts` — Dual-Path Authentication

Authentication supports two paths: HMAC-signed cookies (primary, for magic-link login) and Supabase JWT Bearer tokens (for council/trainer endpoints).

| Mechanism | Cookie Name / Header | Verification Method | Used By |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HMAC Cookie | `gv_admin_session` | `verifySessionToken()` — SHA-256 HMAC, base64url-encoded payload + signature | Magic-link login, most routes |
| Supabase JWT | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` | `supabase.auth.getUser(token)` | Council, trainer, DI routes |

The `AuthUser` interface defines 5 tiers: `anonymous`, `free`, `core`, `pro`, `enterprise` [api/\_lib/auth.ts#13-18](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/auth.ts#L13-L18) The `AdminSessionPayload` encodes `version`, `userId`, `email`, `role`, `tier`, `issuedAt`, and `expiresAt` with a 14-day default TTL [api/\_lib/auth.ts#20-28](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/auth.ts#L20-L28) [api/\_lib/auth.ts#11](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/auth.ts#L11-L11)

Key functions:

- `getAuthUser(req)` — async, tries cookie-first then Supabase JWT. On JWT path, fetches `profiles` table for tier/admin enrichment with a 60s in-memory cache [api/\_lib/auth.ts#368-458](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/auth.ts#L368-L458)
- `signSessionPayload()` / `verifySessionToken()` — HMAC SHA-256 signing using `SESSION_SECRET` env var [api/\_lib/auth.ts#153-204](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/auth.ts#L153-L204)
- `createAuthSessionCookie()` — builds `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Secure` cookie string [api/\_lib/auth.ts#206-237](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/auth.ts#L206-L237)
- `requireAuth()` / `requireAdmin()` / `requireFounderOrAdmin()` — guard helpers that return `AuthUser` or error objects [api/\_lib/auth.ts#465-504](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/auth.ts#L465-L504)
- `isFounderAdminEmail()` — checks against `FOUNDER_ADMIN_EMAILS` env var (defaults to founder email) [api/\_lib/auth.ts#49-57](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/auth.ts#L49-L57)
- Password verification supports both `scrypt` and `pbkdf2` hash formats via `verifyAdminPassword()` [api/\_lib/auth.ts#130-151](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/auth.ts#L130-L151)

Sources: [api/\_lib/auth.ts#1-543](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/auth.ts#L1-L543)

### `cors.ts` — Origin-Aware CORS

`applyCorsHeaders(req, res, options)` sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `Allow-Methods`, `Allow-Headers`, and `Vary` headers. Origins are validated against `CORS_ORIGINS` env var; if the request origin matches a configured origin, it's reflected; otherwise the first configured origin or `*` is used [api/\_lib/cors.ts#41-58](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/cors.ts#L41-L58) [api/\_lib/cors.ts#73-85](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/cors.ts#L73-L85)

Sources: [api/\_lib/cors.ts#1-86](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/cors.ts#L1-L86)

### `requestGuard.ts` — Bot Detection & 2-Tier Rate Limiting

Extracted from a former Next.js-style middleware into reusable helpers for the Vite + Vercel architecture [api/\_lib/requestGuard.ts#1-7](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/requestGuard.ts#L1-L7)

Bot Detection: 15 regex patterns match common bots, crawlers, and security scanners (`curl`, `wget`, `python-requests`, `sqlmap`, `nmap`, etc.). A missing User-Agent is also treated as a bot [api/\_lib/requestGuard.ts#9-25](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/requestGuard.ts#L9-L25) [api/\_lib/requestGuard.ts#58-64](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/requestGuard.ts#L58-L64)

2-Tier Rate Limiting operates via in-memory `Map` structures:

| Tier | Window | Limit | Map |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Per-second burst | 1 second | 5 requests/IP | `secondWindowMap` |
| Per-minute sustained | 60 seconds | 30 requests/IP | `ipWindowMap` |

Rate-limited paths: `/api/billy`, `/api/actions`, `/api/diligence` [api/\_lib/requestGuard.ts#27-31](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/requestGuard.ts#L27-L31) The `checkRateLimit(ip)` function returns `{ allowed, remaining, retryAfter }` [api/\_lib/requestGuard.ts#70-104](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/requestGuard.ts#L70-L104)

Sources: [api/\_lib/requestGuard.ts#1-105](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/requestGuard.ts#L1-L105)

### `rateLimit.ts` — Tier-Based Query Limits

A higher-level rate limiter backed by Supabase (not in-memory). Works per-user (logged in) or per-session (anonymous).

| Tier | Billy Query Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `anonymous` | 2 |
| `free` | 10 |
| `core` | unlimited (-1) |
| `pro` | unlimited (-1) |
| `enterprise` | unlimited (-1) |

`TIER_FEATURES` maps each tier to feature flags: `billyUnlimited`, `claudeAccess`, `plkMemory`, `domainLanes`, `diligenceExports`, `symbioCoderAccess`, `adhdFullAccess`, `collaboratorEngineAccess`, `resumeRockstarAccess` [api/\_lib/rateLimit.ts#32-101](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/rateLimit.ts#L32-L101)

`checkAndIncrementLimit(sessionId, userId?)` atomically reads, checks, and increments the counter. For logged-in users it reads from the `users` table; for anonymous users it reads from `session_rate_limits` with daily window rotation [api/\_lib/rateLimit.ts#151-269](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/rateLimit.ts#L151-L269)

Sources: [api/\_lib/rateLimit.ts#1-319](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/rateLimit.ts#L1-L319)

### `response.ts` — Envelope Pattern

All API responses use a standard `ApiEnvelope`:

```
interface ApiEnvelope {


response: string;


provider: string;


timestamp: string;


free?: boolean;


tokensUsed?: number | null;


processingTime?: number;


metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;


}
```

`envelope(response, provider, options)` builds the envelope [api/\_lib/response.ts#29-61](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/response.ts#L29-L61) `sendJson(res, status, body)` writes JSON with `Content-Type` header and reports 5xx errors to Sentry via `captureApiResponseError()` [api/\_lib/response.ts#19-27](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/response.ts#L19-L27)

Sources: [api/\_lib/response.ts#1-82](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/response.ts#L1-L82)

### `sentry.ts` — Observability Wrapper

Three wrapper patterns:

- `withSentryVercelHandler(handler, routeName)` — wraps a `(req, res) => void` handler with an isolation scope, transaction span, and automatic exception capture [api/\_lib/sentry.ts#87-141](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/sentry.ts#L87-L141)
- `withSentryFetchHandler(handler, routeName)` — same for Fetch API handlers (used by `council/run.ts`) [api/\_lib/sentry.ts#143-201](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/sentry.ts#L143-L201)
- `withSentryCronMonitor(slug, callback, config)` — wraps cron jobs with Sentry monitor check-ins [api/\_lib/sentry.ts#203-215](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/sentry.ts#L203-L215)

Sources: [api/\_lib/sentry.ts#1-216](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/sentry.ts#L1-L216)

## Route Map — Code Entities to API Surface

Sources: All `search_files` results for api/ routes.

## Key Routes — Detailed

### `api/billy.ts` — Main AI Chat with RRF Retrieval

The Billy route is the platform's central chat endpoint (~900 lines). It supports bootstrap greetings, multi-stream retrieval, Gravity Protocol analysis, memory capture, SymbioCoder analysis, and VibeCoder scoring [api/billy.ts#1-14](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L1-L14)

Request flow:

1. Auth & CORS: `applyCorsHeaders()`, `getAuthUser(req)`, resolve tier/embodiment/room [api/billy.ts#482-517](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L482-L517)
2. Session Context: `buildBillySessionSystemPrompt()` loads autobiographies, constitutions, memories [api/billy.ts#557-562](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L557-L562)
3. Bootstrap path: If `body.bootstrap` is set, sends a greeting via `routeLlm()` with `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT` and founder appendix [api/billy.ts#569-663](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L569-L663)
4. Retrieval (5 parallel streams via `Promise.all`):
   - `matchKnowledgeFragments()` — semantic search against `knowledge_fragments` [api/billy.ts#699-703](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L699-L703)
   - `searchKnowledgeFragments()` — full-text search [api/billy.ts#704-708](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L704-L708)
   - `matchSkillFragments()` — semantic search against `skill_fragments` [api/billy.ts#709-713](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L709-L713)
   - `searchSkillFragments()` — full-text search on skills [api/billy.ts#714-718](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L714-L718)
   - `retrieveMemoryEntries()` — persistent memory [api/billy.ts#688-696](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L688-L696)
5. RRF Merge: `rrfMerge()` fuses all 4 fragment streams with weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion (semantic knowledge 1.3, semantic skill 1.1, text knowledge 1.0, text skill 0.9) [api/billy.ts#441-472](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L441-L472)
6. Prompt Assembly: `buildBillyMessages()` from `shared/billy/runtime.ts` [api/billy.ts#815-823](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L815-L823)
7. LLM Call: `routeLlm(prompt, context)` [api/billy.ts#825-828](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L825-L828)
8. Post-processing: Gravity Protocol metadata, SymbioCoder analysis, VibeCoder scoring, memory capture, session logging [api/billy.ts#331-386](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L331-L386)

RRF Merge Detail:

Constants: `DEFAULT_TOP_K = 8`, `MAX_TOP_K = 12`, `MAX_CONTEXT_CHUNKS = 14`, `MAX_SKILL_CHUNKS = 4`, `MAX_MEMORY_ENTRIES = 4` [api/billy.ts#58-65](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L58-L65)

### `api/di.ts` — Multi-Persona DI Chat

The DI endpoint serves conversations with any of the 24 Digital Intelligence personas. It requires a `diSlug` to identify which DI to activate [api/di.ts#101-135](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/di.ts#L101-L135)

Key differences from Billy:

- Loads a `DIProfile` via `getDIProfile(diSlug)` and checks `profileStatus === "active"` [api/di.ts#132-136](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/di.ts#L132-L136)
- Looks up `di_sessions` table for relational state (depth, quirk activations, session thread) [api/di.ts#147-161](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/di.ts#L147-L161)
- Builds messages via `buildDIMessages()` from `shared/di/index.ts` [api/di.ts#245-252](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/di.ts#L245-L252)
- After response: upserts `di_sessions`, evaluates for memory events via `evaluateForMemory()`, writes to `di_memory_events` table [api/di.ts#275-309](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/di.ts#L275-L309)
- Response includes `relationalDepth`, `sessionThread`, `memoryEventWritten` metadata [api/di.ts#311-340](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/di.ts#L311-L340)

Sources: [api/di.ts#1-341](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/di.ts#L1-L341) [api/\_lib/diMemoryPipeline.ts#29-131](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/diMemoryPipeline.ts#L29-L131)

### `api/login.ts` / `api/logout.ts` — Magic Link Auth

Login: POST-only. Validates email against `MAGIC_LINK_ALLOWLIST` (falls back to founder admin emails). Calls Supabase `signInWithOtp()` with `shouldCreateUser: false` [api/login.ts#39-102](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/login.ts#L39-L102)

Logout: POST-only. Calls `clearAdminSessionCookie()` which sets `gv_admin_session` cookie with `Max-Age=0` [api/logout.ts#1-13](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/logout.ts#L1-L13) [api/\_lib/auth.ts#243-257](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/auth.ts#L243-L257)

### `api/gravity.ts` — Gravity Inspector

GET-only, auth-required. Lists stored Two-Pass Gravity Protocol reports and their fragments for the authenticated user. Fragments are sorted by `priority_rank`, `signal_weight`, and `chunk_index`. Returns the `strongestReport` by highest `signal_weight` [api/gravity.ts#1-107](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/gravity.ts#L1-L107)

### `api/diligence.ts` — CSV Diligence Report Parser

GET-only endpoint that reads and parses CSV files from the `Diligence_Reports/` directory on disk. Implements a custom CSV parser (handles quoted fields, escaped quotes) [api/diligence.ts#82-135](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/diligence.ts#L82-L135) Parses 5 data sources in parallel:

| Source | Files Tried | Output Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claim Ledger | `claimledger.csv`, `claim_ledger.csv`, `Claim_Ledger.csv` | `Claim[]` with lane classification |
| Chronology | `chronology.csv`, `Chronology.csv` | `ChronologyEntry[]` |
| Skepticism Register | `skepticismregister.csv`, etc. | `SkepticismEntry[]` |
| Evidence Index | `evidenceindex.csv`, etc. | `EvidenceEntry[]` |
| Architecture Map | `architecturemap.csv`, etc. | `ArchitectureEntry[]` |

Results are cached for 5 minutes (`CACHE_TTL_MS = 300000`) [api/diligence.ts#79-80](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/diligence.ts#L79-L80) Cache can be invalidated via `?refresh=1` query param [api/diligence.ts#325](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/diligence.ts#L325-L325)

Sources: [api/diligence.ts#1-331](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/diligence.ts#L1-L331)

### `api/council/run.ts` — Multi-Persona Council

Uses the Fetch API handler pattern (wrapped with `withSentryFetchHandler`). Accepts `userPrompt`, `slugs` (DI persona slugs), and optional `corpusContext`. Delegates to `runCouncil()` from `server/council/councilRunner.ts` [api/council/run.ts#1-76](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/council/run.ts#L1-L76)

## Cross-Cutting Patterns

### Handler Composition Pattern

Every Vercel function exports a `default async function handler(req, res)`. Instead of middleware chains, each handler composes its needs from `_lib/`:

```
export default async function handler(req, res) {


applyCorsHeaders(req, res, { methods: ["POST", "OPTIONS"], ... });


if (req.method === "OPTIONS") { res.status(200).end(); return; }


if (req.method !== "POST") { sendJson(res, 405, { error: "..." }); return; }


const authUser = await getAuthUser(req);


// ... route logic ...


sendJson(res, 200, envelope(result.response, result.provider, { ... }));


}
```

### Graceful Degradation

Billy's retrieval stack degrades through 3 tiers: semantic → text-only → none. If embedding fails, text search is attempted. If text search also fails, the LLM is called without context [api/billy.ts#682-797](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L682-L797)

### Braintrust Tracing

LLM calls and embedding calls are wrapped with `traceBraintrust()` from `instrument.ts` for observability. Traces include input, output, provider metadata, token counts, and error status [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#120-172](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L120-L172)

Sources: [api/billy.ts#576-605](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L576-L605) [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#120-172](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L120-L172) [api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#85-122](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L85-L122)

# Python Generative Engine & Core Brain

> Reconstruction note: Reconstructed from browser-saved MHT DeepWiki pages in wiki.zip.


**Relevant source files**

- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1)
- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/advanced-evaluation/references/evaluation-pipeline.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/advanced-evaluation/references/evaluation-pipeline.md?plain=1)

The Python backend of GestaltView is a FastAPI server (`server/gestaltview_generative_engine.py`) paired with a modular `server/core/` package that implements a 9-stage consciousness-processing pipeline. This page documents both layers: the HTTP-facing generative engine and the algorithmic "brain" that orchestrates PLK analysis, BucketDrop capture, Loom refinement, Tapestry weaving, Tribunal validation, and blockchain-anchored provenance.

## Architecture Overview

9-Stage Processing Pipeline — Code Entity Map

Sources: [server/gestaltview\_generative\_engine.py#1-24](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/gestaltview_generative_engine.py#L1-L24) [server/core/brain.py#1-15](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L1-L15) [server/core/\_\_init\_\_.py#1-23](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/__init__.py#L1-L23)

## FastAPI Server (`gestaltview_generative_engine.py`)

The generative engine is a single-file FastAPI application started via `uvicorn server.gestaltview_generative_engine:app --reload`. It defines all endpoint routes, data models (Pydantic), and global singletons for the engine subsystems.

### Configuration

The `Config` class reads environment variables and sets feature flags with graceful degradation — if an API key is absent, the corresponding provider is disabled:

| Config field | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ENABLE_OPENAI` | `bool(OPENAI_API_KEY)` | Gate for OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini` calls |
| `ENABLE_GROQ` | `bool(GROQ_API_KEY)` | Gate for Groq `mixtral-8x7b-32768` calls |
| `ENABLE_EMBEDDINGS` | `True` | SentenceTransformer / TF-IDF fallback |
| `ENABLE_WHISPER` | `True` | Audio transcription via Whisper |
| `ENABLE_OCR` | `True` | Image text extraction via Tesseract |
| `EMBEDDING_DIM` | `384` | Vector dimensions for local embeddings |
| `RESONANCE_HIGH_THRESHOLD` | `0.7` | PLK high-resonance gate |
| `RESONANCE_LOW_THRESHOLD` | `0.3` | PLK low-resonance gate |

Sources: [server/gestaltview\_generative\_engine.py#48-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/gestaltview_generative_engine.py#L48-L67)

### Global Singletons & Persistence Bridge

Six global singletons are instantiated at module load time:

```
fusion_engine        = FusionEngine(config)


llm_router           = LLMRouter(config)


blackboard_responder = BlackboardResponder(llm_router, fusion_engine)


resonance_builder    = ResonanceLinkBuilder(fusion_engine)


musical_dna_analyzer = MusicalDNAAnalyzer()


embodiment_manager   = EmbodimentProfileManager()
```

When the `engine_persistence_bridge` module is importable, `embodiment_manager` is replaced with `DatabaseEmbodimentManager` (a Supabase-backed subclass), and persistence hooks (`persist_fusion_drop`, `persist_blackboard_turn`, etc.) are activated. These hooks are fire-and-forget — they catch exceptions internally and never block the endpoint response.

Sources: [server/gestaltview\_generative\_engine.py#790-848](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/gestaltview_generative_engine.py#L790-L848) [server/engine\_persistence\_bridge.py#1-8](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/engine_persistence_bridge.py#L1-L8) [server/core/db\_managers.py#33-91](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/db_managers.py#L33-L91)

### CORS Configuration

The middleware allows three origins: the production Vercel deployment (`gestaltview-v2-dig.vercel.app`), `localhost:5173` (Vite dev), and `localhost:3000`.

Sources: [server/gestaltview\_generative\_engine.py#817-827](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/gestaltview_generative_engine.py#L817-L827)

## Core Brain (`server/core/`)

The `server/core/` package is the algorithmic brain, extracted from a monolithic `GestaltView_Brain_Logic_9_15_25.py` into discrete modules. It is wired to Supabase (`AsyncClient`) and has no SQLite dependency.

### Package Structure

| Module | Primary Class/Functions | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `types.py` | `ConsciousnessState`, `ConsciousnessMetrics`, `BucketDrop`, `PersonalLanguageKey`, `TapestryThread` | Canonical dataclasses and enums |
| `brain.py` | `GestaltViewCore` | 9-stage orchestrator |
| `plk.py` | `PLKEngine` | Linguistic fingerprint builder |
| `bucket_drops.py` | `BucketDropsEngine` | Capture, score, persist thought fragments |
| `loom.py` | `LoomProcessor` | Iterative refinement into structured insights |
| `tapestry.py` | `TapestryWeaver` | Pattern classification and thread synthesis |
| `tribunal.py` | `TribunalValidator` | 5-dimension response validation |
| `provenance.py` | `seal()`, `create_envelope()`, `stamp_envelope()`, etc. | OpenTimestamps blockchain anchoring |
| `provenance_routes.py` | `handle_create()`, `handle_stamp()`, etc. | HTTP route handlers for provenance API |
| `provenance_upgrade_job.py` | `run_upgrade_batch()` | Cron job for Bitcoin block confirmation |
| `db_managers.py` | `DatabaseEmbodimentManager`, `DatabaseSymbioticCore` | Supabase-backed overrides for engine singletons |

Sources: [server/core/\_\_init\_\_.py#1-23](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/__init__.py#L1-L23) [server/core/types.py#1-70](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/types.py#L1-L70)

## The 9-Stage Processing Pipeline

`GestaltViewCore.process()` is the main entry point — an async method that takes `user_input` (string) and optional `context` dict, then runs 9 sequential stages.

Pipeline Sequence Diagram

Sources: [server/core/brain.py#76-136](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L76-L136)

### Stage 1: Detect ConsciousnessState

`_detect_state()` classifies the user's cognitive state from text keyword matching and context flags. It scores each of 7 `ConsciousnessState` enum values and returns the highest-scoring one, defaulting to `REFLECTIVE` if all scores are zero.

| ConsciousnessState | Trigger Keywords / Context Flags |
| --- | --- |
| `HYPERFOCUS` | "can't stop thinking", "tunnel vision", "deep dive", "hyperfocus", "in the zone" |
| `OVERWHELMED` | "too much", "overwhelmed", "can't process", "scattered", "exploded", "chaos" |
| `CREATIVE_FLOW` | "ideas flowing", "inspiration", "jazz", "creative flow" |
| `BREAKTHROUGH` | "aha moment", "breakthrough", "lightning bolt", "clicked", "revelation" |
| `SCATTERED` | `context.task_switching_frequent == True` |
| `REFLECTIVE` | `context.deep_reflection_mode == True` |
| `INTEGRATIVE` | `context.integration_happening == True` |

Each keyword match contributes 2 points; context flags contribute 3 points.

Sources: [server/core/brain.py#140-154](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L140-L154) [server/core/types.py#12-19](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/types.py#L12-L19)

### Stage 2: Init / Update PersonalLanguageKey (PLK)

If no PLK exists for the session, a new `PersonalLanguageKey` dataclass is created. Then `PLKEngine.analyze()` performs four detection passes over the user's text, followed by a resonance score computation.

Sources: [server/core/brain.py#88-92](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L88-L92)

### Stage 3: Capture BucketDrop

`BucketDropsEngine.capture()` creates a `BucketDrop` record with urgency classification, emotional intensity scoring, and cognitive complexity scoring, then persists it to Supabase.

Sources: [server/core/brain.py#94-101](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L94-L101)

### Stage 4: Measure ConsciousnessMetrics

`_measure_metrics()` computes 8 floating-point metrics from the text, the detected state, and PLK resonance. The `overall_coherence` is the mean of `awareness_depth`, `empathetic_resonance`, `cognitive_flexibility`, and `plk_resonance`.

Sources: [server/core/brain.py#156-182](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L156-L182)

### Stage 5: Loom Processing

`LoomProcessor.process()` runs up to 3 iterative refinement passes, stopping early if coherence reaches 0.8.

Sources: [server/core/brain.py#107](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L107-L107)

### Stage 6: Tapestry Weaving

`TapestryWeaver.weave()` classifies the pattern type and synthesises a `TapestryThread`, then upserts a snapshot to `consciousness_profiles`.

Sources: [server/core/brain.py#110](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L110-L110)

### Stage 7: Generate Response

`_generate_response()` builds a contextually grounded response using state-specific opening phrases and Founder-as-Algorithm wisdom.

Sources: [server/core/brain.py#184-203](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L184-L203)

### Stage 8: Tribunal Validation

`TribunalValidator.validate()` scores the AI response on 5 dimensions and persists edge-case results.

Sources: [server/core/brain.py#116-121](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L116-L121)

### Stage 9: Session Impact

`_session_impact()` computes the session duration, coherence delta (relative to 0.5 baseline), and quality classification.

Sources: [server/core/brain.py#227-238](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L227-L238)

### Pipeline Return Shape

The `process()` method returns a dict with these keys:

| Key | Type | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `response` | `str` | Stage 7 |
| `consciousness_state` | `str` | Stage 1 enum value |
| `consciousness_metrics` | `dict` | Stage 4 `ConsciousnessMetrics` as dict |
| `plk_resonance` | `float` | Stage 2 |
| `bucket_drop_id` | `str` | Stage 3 `drop.id` |
| `tapestry` | `dict` | Stage 6 |
| `validation` | `dict` | Stage 8 |
| `session_impact` | `dict` | Stage 9 |
| `founder_patterns` | `list[str]` | Matched Founder-as-Algorithm pattern keys |

Sources: [server/core/brain.py#126-136](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L126-L136)

## GestaltViewCore & Founder-as-Algorithm

`GestaltViewCore` is instantiated once per user session with a `user_id` and `AsyncClient` (Supabase). It owns instances of all five sub-engines.

### Founder-as-Algorithm Patterns (8 Named Weights)

The class constant `FOUNDER_PATTERNS` encodes Keith Soyka's lived experience as 8 named string constants. Each pattern is a short phrase used as contextual wisdom in generated responses and as a matching key against user input.

| Key | Pattern Phrase | Maps to State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `adhd_jazz` | "My ADHD is my jazz — chaotic but with profound rhythm" | `HYPERFOCUS` |
| `chaos_current` | "Your chaos has a current — we navigate it together" | `OVERWHELMED` |
| `exploded_mind` | "Exploded picture mind sees everything at once" | `SCATTERED` |
| `scars_to_code` | "Every difficult chapter became a feature" | `BREAKTHROUGH` |
| `presence_not_perfection` | "Presence, not perfection — honoring where you are" | `REFLECTIVE` |
| `beautiful_tapestry` | "Weaving fragments into a beautiful tapestry" | `CREATIVE_FLOW` |
| `consciousness_serving` | "Technology that serves consciousness, not exploits it" | `INTEGRATIVE` |
| `cognitive_justice` | "Every mind deserves technology that celebrates its uniqueness" | (general match) |

`_match_founder_patterns()` checks if any word (>4 chars) from each pattern phrase appears in the user's input and returns matching keys.

Sources: [server/core/brain.py#46-56](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L46-L56) [server/core/brain.py#205-225](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/brain.py#L205-L225)

## PLKEngine — Personal Language Key

`PLKEngine` in `server/core/plk.py` is a stateless engine that builds, evolves, and scores a user's linguistic fingerprint. It receives a `PersonalLanguageKey` and returns a mutated copy. The TypeScript counterpart (`shared/llm/plk.ts`) provides PLK-aware system prompt building on the frontend.

### PersonalLanguageKey Dataclass

Defined in `server/core/types.py`:

| Field | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user_id` | `str` | Owner |
| `metaphors` | `Dict[str, Any]` | Accumulated metaphor category → count |
| `communication_patterns` | `Dict[str, float]` | Question frequency, exclamation intensity, self-reflection markers |
| `emotional_markers` | `Dict[str, Any]` | Emotion → accumulated score |
| `cognitive_style` | `str` | Detected style (e.g. `"ADHD_flow"`, `"systematic_processing"`) |
| `authenticity_score` | `float` | 0–1 richness indicator |
| `resonance_history` | `List[float]` | Historical resonance scores |

Sources: [server/core/types.py#49-57](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/types.py#L49-L57)

### Analysis Pipeline (`PLKEngine.analyze`)

`analyze()` performs four sequential detection passes on user text:

1. `_detect_metaphors()` — Scans for 4 metaphor categories (`mind_metaphors`, `chaos_metaphors`, `flow_metaphors`, `building_metaphors`) containing 14+ patterns. Increments category counters.
2. `_detect_communication_patterns()` — Measures question frequency (`?/word_count`), exclamation intensity (`!/word_count`), uncertainty markers, certainty markers, and self-reflection markers.
3. `_detect_emotional_markers()` — Scans 4 emotion categories (vulnerability, excitement, curiosity, empathy) with 4 keywords each. Accumulates scores.
4. `_detect_cognitive_style()` — Classifies as `ADHD_flow` (>2 ADHD indicators hit), `systematic_processing`, `creative_divergent`, or `adaptive_integration`.

After the four passes, `_calculate_authenticity()` produces a 0–1 score based on PLK data richness (0.25 per populated category).

Sources: [server/core/plk.py#38-122](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/plk.py#L38-L122)

### Resonance Scoring (`PLKEngine.score_resonance`)

Returns a 0.0–1.0 float. If the PLK has no data yet, returns 0.5 (neutral baseline). Otherwise computes `raw = keyword_hits / total_checks` across all metaphor and emotional patterns, then blends: `blended = raw * 0.6 + authenticity_score * 0.4`.

Sources: [server/core/plk.py#51-75](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/plk.py#L51-L75)

### Enhanced PLK (Generative Engine Layer)

The generative engine file also contains `EnhancedPersonalLanguageKey` — a Pydantic-based PLK implementation used for prompt enrichment. It operates on a `PLKProfile` (with `signature_metaphors`, `energy_words`, `avoidance_words`, `idiolect_patterns`) and computes resonance with a breakdown by category. The `enrich_prompt()` method injects a `[PLK_CONTEXT]` block into LLM prompts containing the user's linguistic markers.

Sources: [server/gestaltview\_generative\_engine.py#320-384](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/gestaltview_generative_engine.py#L320-L384)

## BucketDropsEngine — Urgency Classification & Connections

`BucketDropsEngine` in `server/core/bucket_drops.py` handles the capture and persistence of thought fragments (BucketDrops). It writes to Supabase `bucket_drops` and fires a provenance seal in the background.

### BucketDrop Dataclass

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `str` | UUID |
| `content` | `str` | Raw text |
| `urgency` | `str` | `random` / `regular` / `critical` / `lightning` |
| `timestamp` | `datetime` | Capture time |
| `consciousness_state` | `ConsciousnessState` | State at capture time |
| `emotional_intensity` | `float` | 0–100 score |
| `cognitive_complexity` | `float` | Sentence length + complexity marker score |
| `resonance_score` | `float` | PLK authenticity score |
| `connections` | `List[str]` | Related drop IDs |
| `metadata` | `Dict[str, Any]` | Context pass-through |

Sources: [server/core/types.py#35-45](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/types.py#L35-L45)

### Urgency Classification

`_classify_urgency()` checks the content against a keyword hierarchy. The first level that matches wins:

| Level | Keywords |
| --- | --- |
| `lightning` | "urgent", "critical", "immediately", "right now", "asap", "lightning" |
| `critical` | "important", "must", "essential", "priority", "deadline" |
| `regular` | "should", "need to", "want to", "plan to" |
| `random` | (fallback — no keywords) |

Sources: [server/core/bucket\_drops.py#30-35](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/bucket_drops.py#L30-L35) [server/core/bucket\_drops.py#88-93](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/bucket_drops.py#L88-L93)

### Jaccard Similarity for Connections

`find_connections()` computes word-level Jaccard similarity between a new drop and recent drops. Pairs with Jaccard ≥ 0.15 are considered connected:

```
jaccard = |words_a ∩ words_b| / |words_a ∪ words_b|
```

Sources: [server/core/bucket\_drops.py#71-84](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/bucket_drops.py#L71-L84)

### Scoring Functions

- `_score_emotional_intensity()` — Starts at 50.0, adds 10.0 per high-intensity marker (e.g. `"!!!"`, `"absolutely"`, `"devastating"`), subtracts 5.0 per low-intensity marker (e.g. `"maybe"`, `"perhaps"`). Clamped to [0, 100].
- `_score_cognitive_complexity()` — `avg_words_per_sentence * 2 + marker_count * 5`, capped at 100. Complexity markers: "however", "therefore", "consequently", "moreover", "furthermore".

Sources: [server/core/bucket\_drops.py#95-110](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/bucket_drops.py#L95-L110)

### Provenance Seal (Fire-and-Forget)

After a successful Supabase insert, `_persist()` constructs a sanitized `seal_obj` (with schema `gsvw.bucket-drop.v1`) and calls `provenance.seal()` in a background thread via `asyncio.create_task(asyncio.to_thread(...))`. The provenance seal never blocks the user-facing response — failures are logged but not surfaced.

Sources: [server/core/bucket\_drops.py#112-173](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/bucket_drops.py#L112-L173)

## LoomProcessor — Iterative Refinement

`LoomProcessor` in `server/core/loom.py` runs up to `MAX_ITERATIONS = 3` refinement passes over a BucketDrop to extract patterns, gaps, threads, and motifs. It halts early when `coherence_score >= 0.8`.

### Refinement Pass Structure

Each `_refine_pass()` extracts four categories of insight:

| Category | Markers | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patterns | "always", "never", "every time", "pattern", "cycle", "recurring" | Detected on every iteration |
| Gaps | "don't know", "unsure", "missing", "gap", "unclear", "need to figure" | Detected on every iteration |
| Threads | "because", "therefore", "leads to", "connects", "related to" | Only detected when `overall_coherence > 0.6` |
| Motifs | "again", "still", "back to", "reminds me", "like before" | Only detected on iteration ≥ 1 (deeper passes) |

Sources: [server/core/loom.py#66-103](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/loom.py#L66-L103)

### Coherence Calculation

`_calculate_coherence()` computes a composite score:

```
coherence = metrics.overall_coherence * 0.1


+ min(patterns * 0.1, 0.3)


+ min(threads * 0.15, 0.4)


+ min(motifs * 0.1, 0.2)
```

The 0.8 threshold triggers early stopping. If a `run_id` is provided, annotations are persisted to the `loom_annotations` table.

Sources: [server/core/loom.py#105-135](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/loom.py#L105-L135)

Loom Iteration Flow

Sources: [server/core/loom.py#27-62](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/loom.py#L27-L62)

## TapestryWeaver — Pattern Classification

`TapestryWeaver` in `server/core/tapestry.py` synthesizes Loom insights and ConsciousnessMetrics into a `TapestryThread`, then upserts a snapshot to the `consciousness_profiles` table.

### Pattern Classification (`_classify_pattern`)

| Pattern Type | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| `integrative-synthesis` | `cognitive_flexibility > 0.7` AND threads exist |
| `creative-burst` | `creative_consciousness > 0.7` |
| `deep-reflection` | `awareness_depth > 0.7` |

Sources: [server/core/tapestry.py#70-83](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/tapestry.py#L70-L83)

### TapestryThread Dataclass

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `str` | UUID |
| `user_id` | `str` | Owner |

## TribunalValidator — 5-Dimension Scoring

`TribunalValidator` in `server/core/tribunal.py` validates AI responses against consciousness metrics and PLK resonance. It writes to Supabase `tribunal_events` and `tribunal_evidence`.

### Validation Dimensions

The 5 dimensions scored in `_score_dimensions()`:

| Dimension | Scoring Logic | Source Metric |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `authenticity` | Base 0.5; +0.2 for empathic phrases ("i understand", "i hear"), −0.2 for hollow affirmations ("absolutely!", "great question!") | Direct text analysis |
| `consciousness_alignment` | `metrics.overall_coherence` | `ConsciousnessMetrics` |
| `plk_resonance` | `plk_resonance` float from Stage 2 | PLK score passthrough |
| `ethical_coherence` | `metrics.empathetic_resonance` | `ConsciousnessMetrics` |
| `user_sovereignty` | `metrics.embodied_presence` | `ConsciousnessMetrics` |

The overall score is the arithmetic mean of all 5 dimensions. Validation passes if `overall >= 0.7`.

The hollow affirmation penalty (`-0.2` for phrases like "Absolutely!" and "Great question!") is a deliberate anti-sycophancy mechanism.

Sources: [server/core/tribunal.py#24-31](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/tribunal.py#L24-L31) [server/core/tribunal.py#79-99](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/tribunal.py#L79-L99)

### Persistence Policy

Events are only persisted to Supabase for edge cases: validation score `< 0.7` (failures) or `> 0.95` (high-confidence passes). Mid-range validations are not stored, reducing database noise.

When persisted, the event includes a `tribunal_events` row (with triggering agent `"GestaltViewCore"`) and linked `tribunal_evidence` rows (capped at 10 fragment IDs).

Sources: [server/core/tribunal.py#62-131](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/tribunal.py#L62-L131)

### TypeScript Tribunal Counterpart

The TypeScript `evaluateTribunal()` in `shared/tribunal/evaluate.ts` uses a different scoring formula focused on multi-candidate evaluation: 50% evidence alignment (keyword overlap with corpus fragments), 25% PLK resonance (regex signal match), 25% safety (penalty for guarantee/cure/promise language). It also detects unsafe patterns and selects a winning candidate by highest `overallScore`.

Sources: [shared/tribunal/evaluate.ts#19-96](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/tribunal/evaluate.ts#L19-L96)

## Provenance — OpenTimestamps Blockchain Anchoring

The `server/core/provenance.py` module implements a full provenance lifecycle: canonicalization → hashing → envelope creation → OTS calendar stamping → Bitcoin block upgrade → verification.

### Security Contract

> Only the SHA-256 digest is ever sent to OpenTimestamps calendar nodes. Private content never leaves the server.

Sources: [server/core/provenance.py#14-15](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/provenance.py#L14-L15)

### Provenance Lifecycle

Provenance State Machine

Sources: [server/core/provenance.py#83-168](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/provenance.py#L83-L168) [server/core/provenance.py#182-258](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/provenance.py#L182-L258) [server/core/provenance.py#263-345](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/provenance.py#L263-L345) [server/core/provenance.py#350-379](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/provenance.py#L350-L379)

### Key Functions

| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `canonicalize(obj)` | RFC-8785-style deterministic JSON bytes (sorted keys, no whitespace) |
| `hash_canonical(bytes)` | SHA-256 digest as `"sha256:<hex>"` |
| `create_envelope(...)` | Write `provenance_envelopes` row with content hash, context hashes, interpretation bounds, OTS status "pending" |
| `stamp_envelope(id)` | POST raw 32-byte digest to OTS calendar, store `.ots` receipt in Supabase Storage `provenance-receipts` bucket |
| `upgrade_envelope(id)` | Resubmit receipt for Bitcoin block attestation (call 2-3 hours after stamp) |
| `verify_envelope(id, obj)` | Re-canonicalize and compare hash against stored `content_hash` |
| `get_summary(type, id)` | Agent-safe context contract — no raw receipt bytes, only epistemic metadata |
| `seal(...)` | Convenience: `create_envelope()` + `stamp_envelope()` in one call |

Sources: [server/core/provenance.py#65-461](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/provenance.py#L65-L461)

### OTS Calendar Endpoints

Three calendar servers are configured:

1. `https://alice.btc.calendar.opentimestamps.org`
2. `https://bob.btc.calendar.opentimestamps.org`
3. `https://finney.calendar.eternitywall.com`

The stamping function iterates through calendars and stops on the first successful submission.

### Envelope JSON Structure

Each provenance envelope includes:

- `schema`: `"gsvw.provenance-envelope.v1"`
- `content_hash`: SHA-256 of canonicalized content
- `context_hashes`: Array of `{role, subject_id, hash}` for related inputs
- `interpretation_bounds`: `{may_summarize, may_infer_identity, may_export, requires_user_review}`
- `ots`: Status tracking (pending/upgraded/verified), receipt path, calendar URLs, Bitcoin attestation
- `lineage`: Parent envelopes and derived artifacts

Sources: [server/core/provenance.py#114-148](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/provenance.py#L114-L148)

### Upgrade Job

`provenance_upgrade_job.py` is a batch job (runnable via `python -m server.core.provenance_upgrade_job` or a cron trigger). It finds up to 20 pending envelopes older than 90 minutes (approximately 9 Bitcoin blocks) and attempts to upgrade each.

Sources: [server/core/provenance\_upgrade\_job.py#1-79](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/provenance_upgrade_job.py#L1-L79)

`provenance_routes.py` exposes HTTP handlers for the provenance API:

## FusionEngine — Multimodal Processing

`FusionEngine` in the generative engine file handles text, image, audio, and video inputs through a lazy-loaded pipeline:

| Modality | Processing | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TEXT` | Direct text fusion + embedding | SentenceTransformer (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) or TF-IDF fallback |
| `IMAGE` | OCR via Tesseract | `pytesseract`, `PIL` |
| `AUDIO` | Whisper transcription | `whisper` (tiny model) |
| `VIDEO` | Falls through to audio processing | Same as audio |

The `_lazy_load()` method initializes models only on first use. The `embed_text()` method attempts SentenceTransformer first, then falls back to sklearn TF-IDF with zero-padding to `EMBEDDING_DIM` (384).

Sources: [server/gestaltview\_generative\_engine.py#154-258](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/gestaltview_generative_engine.py#L154-L258)

## LLMRouter — Provider Cascade

The Python `LLMRouter` implements a provider cascade within the generative engine:

The cascade order is: Local LLM → Groq → OpenAI → Deterministic fallback. If PLK injection is enabled and a profile exists, the prompt is wrapped in a `[PLK_CONTEXT]` block before being sent to any provider.

Sources: [server/gestaltview\_generative\_engine.py#420-548](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/gestaltview_generative_engine.py#L420-L548)

## Blackboard Responder & Persona Prompts

`BlackboardResponder` handles the `/api/blackboard/respond` endpoint. It selects a persona-specific system prompt from `PERSONA_PROMPTS` (7 built-in personas), creates an `LLMRequest`, and generates a response with a `ProvenanceEnvelope`.

| Persona Slug | Identity |
| --- | --- |
| `billy` | Thread-keeper; holds continuity, asks one question at a time |
| `the-weaver` | Sees patterns; speaks in loom/tapestry metaphors |
| `the-guardian` | Holds boundaries; compass, not critic |
| `the-architect` | Sees structure in chaos; proposes, doesn't impose |
| `gate-keeper` | Manages provenance; asks "where from, where going?" |
| `the-keeper` | Sanctuary guardian; gentle, slow, no agenda |
| `the-curator` | Creation Corner steward; enthusiastic, precise, sees raw material |

Sources: [server/gestaltview\_generative\_engine.py#554-638](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/gestaltview_generative_engine.py#L554-L638)

## SymbioticFeedbackCore — Adaptive Learning

`SymbioticFeedbackCore` maintains a per-user history of `InteractionRecord` objects (multi-modal input + AI output + user feedback + input vector). It supports:

- `learn_from_interaction()` — Records interaction with feedback score clamped to [0, 1].
- `predict_user_need()` — Finds the most similar historical interaction using `cosine_similarity * 0.5 + user_feedback * 0.5`, returning the prior AI output if the combined score exceeds 0.3.
- `get_faithfulness_level()` — Returns 0.2 (< 5 interactions), 0.5 (< 20), or 0.8 (≥ 20).

`DatabaseSymbioticCore` extends this with Supabase persistence, logging `di_memory_events` after each interaction and bootstrapping from `memory_entries` for returning users.

Sources: [server/gestaltview\_generative\_engine.py#264-314](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/gestaltview_generative_engine.py#L264-L314) [server/core/db\_managers.py#93-142](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/db_managers.py#L93-L142)

## Creation Corner Engine

The `creation_corner_engine.py` module adds a `creation_corner_router` (FastAPI `APIRouter`) with synthesis, artifact-type listing, and health endpoints. It integrates `FusionEngine`, `LLMRouter`, `EnhancedPersonalLanguageKey`, and `HuggingFaceAdapter` for image/audio generation. The synthesis pipeline:

1. Build fusion inputs from text/image/audio
2. Run `FusionEngine.process()`
3. Compute PLK resonance
4. Persist fusion drop via bridge
5. Route to type-specific generator (markdown, image, audio, blueprint, code, etc.)
6. Attach provenance envelope and persist artifact

Sources: [server/creation\_corner\_engine.py#1-207](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/creation_corner_engine.py#L1-L207)

The codebase contains two PLK implementations serving different layers:

The `PLKEngine` tracks metaphors, communication patterns, emotional markers, and cognitive style through iterative analysis passes. The `EnhancedPersonalLanguageKey` operates on pre-built profiles with signature metaphors (weighted), energy words (boost), and avoidance words (penalty), producing a resonance breakdown and prompt context block.

# LLM Router & Multi-Provider Cascade

**Relevant source files**

- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1)

This page documents the multi-provider LLM routing system, the embedding subsystem, Braintrust tracing, and the persistent memory layer. Together, these modules form the backbone of Billy's intelligence pipeline: every user message is routed through a cost-optimized provider cascade, embedded for semantic retrieval, and matched against the user's persistent memory.

Provider Cascade Architecture

## The LLM Router (`api/_lib/llmRouter.ts`)

### Core Interfaces

The router operates on two primary types:

- `LlmContext` — input context carrying `userId`, `mode`, `exhibit`, `plk` (Personal Language Key profile), `systemPrompt`, and `tier` (one of the `BillyTier` values: `anonymous | free | core | pro | enterprise | founder`).
- `LlmResult` — output envelope containing `response`, `provider` name, `timestamp`, `free` flag, `tokensUsed`, `processingTime`, and a `metadata` bag.

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#11-28](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L11-L28)

The seven providers are typed as `ProviderId`:

```
type ProviderId =


| "ollama" | "groq" | "huggingface" | "openrouter"


| "gemini" | "anthropic" | "openai";
```

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#30-37](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L30-L37)

Sources: [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#11-37](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L11-L37) [shared/billy/types.ts#70-74](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/types.ts#L70-L74)

### Provider Cascade Order

The cascade is defined in `CASCADE_ORDER` and the `PROVIDERS` array. Providers are tried in order; the first to succeed wins. Free/local providers are tried first to minimize cost:

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#59-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L59-L67)

| Order | Provider ID | Free? | Default Model | API Format | Env Keys (primary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `ollama` | ✅ | `qwen2.5-coder:7b` | `/api/chat` (Ollama native) | `BILLY_OLLAMA_URL`, `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` |
| 2 | `groq` | ✅ | `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` | OpenAI-compatible | `GROQ_API_KEY` |
| 3 | `huggingface` | ✅ | `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3` | Inference API | `HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY`, `HF_API_TOKEN` |
| 4 | `openrouter` | ✅ | `google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free` | OpenAI-compatible | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| 5 | `gemini` | ✅ | `gemini-2.0-flash` | Google AI `generateContent` | `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` |
| 6 | `anthropic` | ❌ | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Anthropic Messages API | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_API_KEY` |
| 7 | `openai` | ❌ | `gpt-4o-mini` | OpenAI Chat Completions | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |

The `free` flag on each `ProviderDef` is hardcoded in the `PROVIDERS` array: the first five providers are marked `free: true`, while Anthropic and OpenAI are `free: false`.

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#449-492](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L449-L492)

### Provider Configuration Detection

The `isConfigured()` function checks for provider-specific environment variables. Each provider accepts multiple env key variants (including `VITE_*` prefixed keys for client-side builds):

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#174-194](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L174-L194)

For example, Ollama is configured when any of `BILLY_OLLAMA_URL`, `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`, `OLLAMA_HOST`, `OLLAMA_API_URL`, or `OLLAMA_URL` is set. If no env key is set, the provider is skipped in the cascade.

Sources: [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#174-194](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L174-L194)

### Provider Call Implementations

Each provider has a dedicated call function. All share `temperature: 0.4` and are wrapped in `withRetry()` for 429 handling.

`callOllama` — Local inference via the Ollama REST API at `/api/chat`. Defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:11434`. Uses `stream: false`. Token count derived from `prompt_eval_count + eval_count`.

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#413-447](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L413-L447)

`callGroq` and `callOpenAI` — Both use `callOpenAICompat()`, a shared helper that posts to any OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint with Bearer auth.

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#264-300](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L264-L300) [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#302-306](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L302-L306) [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#342-347](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L342-L347)

`callHuggingFace` — Uses the Inference API with Mistral instruction template (`<s>[INST] ... [/INST]`). Estimates tokens via whitespace splitting since HuggingFace doesn't return usage metadata.

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#385-411](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L385-L411)

`callOpenRouter` — OpenAI-compatible with extra headers `HTTP-Referer` and `X-Title` for provider attribution.

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#308-340](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L308-L340)

`callGemini` — Uses the Google AI `generateContent` REST endpoint directly, with a `systemInstruction` field and `maxOutputTokens: 2048`.

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#234-262](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L234-L262)

`callAnthropic` — Uses the Anthropic Messages API with `x-api-key` header and `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`. Token count is `input_tokens + output_tokens`.

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#349-383](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L349-L383)

### Retry on 429

The `withRetry()` function provides a single-retry mechanism specifically for HTTP 429 (rate limited) responses. It catches errors, checks for `429` in the message via regex, sleeps 1 second, then retries once. Non-429 errors are re-thrown immediately.

```
async function withRetry(call: () => Promise<ProviderResult>): Promise<ProviderResult> {


try {


return await call();


} catch (error) {


const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);


if (!/429/.test(message)) throw error;


await sleep(1000);


return call();


}


}
```

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#223-232](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L223-L232)

### The `routeLlm()` Function

`routeLlm()` is the main entry point. It:

1. Returns a test-mode stub when `NODE_ENV === "test"` — [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#572-594](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L572-L594)
2. Filters `PROVIDERS` to only those passing `isConfigured()` — [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#597](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L597-L597)
3. Returns `offlineFallback()` if zero providers are configured — [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#599-607](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L599-L607)
4. Iterates configured providers in cascade order, attempting each — [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#623-659](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L623-L659)
5. On success, returns an `LlmResult` with provider metadata and processing time — [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#626-655](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L626-L655)
6. On failure, records the error in `providerErrors` and moves to the next — [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#656-658](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L656-L658)
7. After all providers fail, returns `offlineFallback()` — [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#661-675](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L661-L675)

### System Prompt Construction

`buildSystemPrompt()` assembles the system prompt from context:

1. Uses `context.systemPrompt` if provided, else `DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` ("You are Billy from GestaltView...")
2. Appends operational mode and user tier
3. Wraps with PLK constraints via `buildPlkSystemPrompt()` if `context.plk` is set

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#106-118](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L106-L118) [api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#55-57](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L55-L57)

The PLK (Personal Language Key) system injects trauma-informed, ADHD-friendly pacing constraints: "Preserve the user's exact words. Never paraphrase. Never compress."

[shared/llm/plk.ts#7-14](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/llm/plk.ts#L7-L14) [shared/llm/plk.ts#20-33](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/llm/plk.ts#L20-L33)

### Offline Fallback

When no providers succeed, `offlineFallback()` returns a deterministic response preserving the user's input text (up to 1200 chars, extracted via `cleanPrompt()`). The provider is reported as `"offline-fallback"` with `free: true` and zero processing time.

## Integration with Billy API

Sources: [api/billy.ts#19-23](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L19-L23) [api/billy.ts#682-806](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L682-L806) [api/billy.ts#882-891](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L882-L891) [api/billy.ts#904-910](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L904-L910)

The `api/billy.ts` handler imports `routeLlm` and calls it after retrieval and prompt assembly. The call passes the assembled system prompt (from `buildBillySessionSystemPrompt()` enriched with SymbioCoder analysis), the user tier, and the PLK profile:

[api/billy.ts#882-891](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L882-L891)

### RRF Merge in Billy

The `rrfMerge()` function in `api/billy.ts` applies Reciprocal Rank Fusion across four retrieval streams with differentiated weights:

| Stream | Weight | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Semantic knowledge fragments | 1.3 | `matchKnowledgeFragments()` via pgvector |
| Text knowledge fragments | 1.0 | `searchKnowledgeFragments()` via text search |
| Semantic skill fragments | 1.1 | `matchSkillFragments()` via pgvector |
| Text skill fragments | 0.9 | `searchSkillFragments()` via text search |

The RRF formula per chunk: `score = weight / (k + rank + 1)`, with `k = 60`.

[api/billy.ts#441-472](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L441-L472)

## Braintrust Tracing

All provider calls and the top-level `routeLlm()` are wrapped in `traceBraintrust()`. This function is defined in `instrument.js` and provides observability through the [Braintrust](https://braintrust.dev/) logging platform.

### Initialization

`initRuntimeBraintrust()` checks for `BRAINTRUST_API_KEY` and `BRAINTRUST_ENABLED`. When enabled, it calls `initLogger()` from the `braintrust` SDK with a project name defaulting to `"GestaltView"`.

[instrument.js#110-135](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/instrument.js#L110-L135)

### Span Tracing

`traceBraintrust()` wraps an async callback. If no Braintrust logger is active, it calls the callback with `null` span (no-op). Otherwise, it uses `logger.traced()` to create a span:

[instrument.js#145-152](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/instrument.js#L145-L152)

In `llmRouter.ts`, `traceProviderCall()` logs:

- Input: system + user messages
- Output: response text
- Metrics: token count, latency
- Metadata: provider name, model, status (success/error)

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#120-172](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L120-L172)

The top-level `routeLlm()` creates a span named `"routeLlm"` of type `"task"`, recording which providers were attempted and which succeeded.

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#559-570](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L559-L570)

## Embedding System (`api/_lib/embeddings.ts`)

### Three-Backend Architecture

The embedding module provides `embedTextForRetrieval()`, the single entry point for generating 768-dimensional embeddings used across the entire system (knowledge retrieval, memory indexing, skill fragment search).

Embedding Backend Selection

Sources: [api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#239-260](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L239-L260) [api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#53-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L53-L67)

| Backend | Default Model | API Endpoint | Env Selection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gemini` | `text-embedding-004` | `generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta` | Default when no HF keys |
| `ollama` | `embeddinggemma` | `{BILLY_OLLAMA_URL}/api/embed` | `BILLY_EMBED_BACKEND=ollama` |
| `huggingface` | `google/embeddinggemma-300m` | `api-inference.huggingface.co` | `BILLY_EMBED_BACKEND=hf` or HF keys present |

[api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#16-17](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L16-L17) [api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#73-122](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L73-L122) [api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#124-163](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L124-L163) [api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#166-237](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L166-L237)

### L2 Normalization

All embeddings are L2-normalized before returning via `normalizeEmbedding()`. This ensures consistent cosine-similarity computation against the pgvector index:

```
function normalizeEmbedding(embedding: number[] | null): number[] | null {


// ... dimension check against BILLY_EMBED_DIMENSIONS ...


const norm = Math.sqrt(embedding.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value * value, 0));


if (!Number.isFinite(norm) || norm === 0) return embedding;


return embedding.map((value) => value / norm);


}
```

The optional `BILLY_EMBED_DIMENSIONS` env var enables a strict dimension check — embeddings that don't match the expected length are rejected (returned as `null`).

[api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#53-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L53-L67)

### Robust Payload Extraction

The HuggingFace backend uses `extractEmbeddingVector()` to handle various response shapes — flat arrays, nested arrays, or `{embedding: [...]}` / `{embeddings: [...]}` / `{data: [...]}` wrappers.

[api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#27-51](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L27-L51)

### Inline Embedding in llmRouter.ts

Note that `llmRouter.ts` also exports `embedQuery()` which provides a separate Gemini-only embedding path using `text-embedding-gemma3` as primary and `text-embedding-004` as fallback. This function is used for in-router embedding needs, while `embedTextForRetrieval()` from `embeddings.ts` is the canonical embedding function used in retrieval pipelines.

[api/\_lib/llmRouter.ts#499-544](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/llmRouter.ts#L499-L544)

## Memory System (`api/_lib/memory.ts`)

### Overview

The memory system provides persistent, per-user memory storage with auto-capture from conversations, hybrid retrieval (semantic + text search with RRF merging), and collaboration memory support.

Memory System Data Flow

Sources: [api/\_lib/memory.ts#299-351](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L299-L351) [api/\_lib/memory.ts#432-520](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L432-L520) [api/\_lib/memory.ts#522-591](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L522-L591)

### 8 Memory Kinds

The system defines eight memory kinds in `MEMORY_KINDS`:

[api/\_lib/memory.ts#20-29](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L20-L29)

| Kind | Description | Auto-capture pattern (regex) | Default importance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | Who the user is | "my name is", "i'm a", "i am someone who" | 4 |
| `preference` | Likes, dislikes, work styles | "i prefer", "i like", "i hate", "i work best when" | 4 |
| `goal` | Intentions and plans | "my goal is", "i want to", "i need to", "i plan to" | 5 |
| `project` | Active work threads | "i'm building", "i'm working on", "my project" | 4 |
| `relationship` | People in user's life | "my wife/husband/partner/son/daughter/..." | 4 |
| `constraint` | Struggles and limitations | "i struggle with", "i get overwhelmed", "i can't focus" | 4 |
| `insight` | Realizations | "i realized", "i noticed", "i learned" | 3 |
| `note` | Default/fallback kind | (not auto-captured) | 3 |

[api/\_lib/memory.ts#76-132](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L76-L132)

### 3 Memory Scopes

Memories are scoped to one of three levels defined in `MEMORY_SCOPES`:

[api/\_lib/memory.ts#33-35](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L33-L35)

| Scope | Usage |
| --- | --- |
| `personal` | Default for auto-captured Billy memories |
| `session` | Session-lived memories |
| `shared` | Collaboration/codex memories (scope `"shared"`, source starts with `"codex-"`) |

### Auto-Capture via Regex (`extractBillyMemoryCandidates`)

`extractBillyMemoryCandidates()` processes a user message and returns up to `AUTO_MEMORY_MAX_CANDIDATES` (2) candidates per message.

The function:

1. Splits the user message into sentences via `splitMemorySentences()` — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#210-221](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L210-L221)
2. Filters out sentences shorter than 24 chars (`AUTO_MEMORY_MIN_CHARS`) — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#310](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L310-L310)
3. Skips question-like sentences (ending in `?` or starting with interrogative words) — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#311](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L311-L311) [api/\_lib/memory.ts#71-72](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L71-L72)
4. Skips volatile support requests ("can you", "help me", "fix this") — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#312](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L312-L312) [api/\_lib/memory.ts#73-74](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L73-L74)
5. Tests remaining sentences against `MEMORY_CAPTURE_RULES` — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#314](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L314-L314)
6. Deduplicates via SHA-256 content hash — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#320-321](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L320-L321)
7. Truncates to 480 chars (`AUTO_MEMORY_MAX_CHARS`) — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#317](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L317-L317)
8. Tags with `"billy-auto"`, the kind, and contextual tags — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#330-335](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L330-L335)

[api/\_lib/memory.ts#299-351](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L299-L351)

Sources: [api/\_lib/memory.ts#68-70](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L68-L70) [api/\_lib/memory.ts#210-351](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L210-L351)

### Hybrid Semantic + Text Search with RRF (`retrieveMemoryEntries`)

The `retrieveMemoryEntries()` function implements hybrid retrieval:

1. If `textOnly` is false and no pre-computed embedding exists, calls `embedTextForRetrieval()` — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#468-473](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L468-L473)
2. If an embedding is available, runs `matchMemoryEntries()` (semantic/pgvector) and `searchMemoryEntries()` (text search) in parallel — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#476-491](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L476-L491)
3. Merges results via `mergeMemoryRows()` using RRF — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#497](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L497-L497)
4. Falls back to text-only search if no embedding available — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#504-519](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L504-L519)

The `mergeMemoryRows()` function implements RRF with `k = 40`:

- Semantic results weighted at 1.2
- Text results weighted at 1.0
- Each memory also gets bonus scores: `importance * 0.01` and `0.08` if pinned

[api/\_lib/memory.ts#398-430](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L398-L430)

The `retrievalMode` field in `MemorySearchResult` reports which path was taken: `"semantic"`, `"text"`, `"text-only"`, or `"none"`.

[api/\_lib/memory.ts#37-42](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L37-L42)

Sources: [api/\_lib/memory.ts#398-520](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L398-L520)

### Memory Persistence (`captureBillyMemories`)

`captureBillyMemories()` orchestrates the full capture flow:

1. Calls `extractBillyMemoryCandidates()` to find candidates
2. For each candidate, computes an embedding via `embedTextForRetrieval()` on the concatenation of title + summary + content — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#548-549](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L548-L549)
3. Upserts into the `memory_entries` table via `upsertMemoryEntry()`, which uses Supabase's `on_conflict=user_id,content_hash` for deduplication — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#563-577](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L563-L577)
4. Memories with importance ≥ 5 are auto-pinned — [api/\_lib/memory.ts#576](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L576-L576)

The function is called fire-and-forget from `api/billy.ts` after the LLM response is generated:

[api/billy.ts#904-910](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L904-L910)

## Billy Memory Pipeline (`api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts`)

The `billyMemoryPipeline.ts` module builds a rich identity context block injected into Billy's system prompt at session start. It also handles session closeout memory extraction.

### `buildBillySessionSystemPrompt()`

This function assembles the session system prompt by fetching multiple Supabase tables in parallel:

1. Billy's `agents` row
2. Billy's `embodiment_profiles` row
3. Billy's `agent_constitutions` row
4. `agent_memory_records` (up to 20, ordered by salience)
5. `agent_memories` (up to 10 summaries)
6. User's `memory_entries` (up to 8)
7. User's `founder_context` row
8. Billy's `agent_autobiographies` row
9. User's `identity_subjects` row

These are assembled via `composeIdentityContextBlock()` into a structured text block with sections: `WHO I AM`, `WHAT I KNOW ABOUT YOU`, `WHAT WE HAVE WORKED ON`, `STANDING CONTEXT`, and `MY CURRENT CHAPTER`. This is prepended to the base system prompt.

[api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#675-769](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L675-L769)

### `recordBillySessionCloseout()`

Called fire-and-forget after each Billy response, this function:

1. Extracts memory candidates from the transcript via `extractSessionMemoryCandidates()` — classifying sentences into `procedural`, `relational`, `semantic`, or `episodic` memory kinds
2. Writes candidates to `agent_memory_records`
3. Writes a session summary to `agent_memories`

[api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#771-887](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L771-L887)
