## 5-Phase Roadmap

The voice pipeline follows a 5-phase development roadmap defined in [billy\_voice/README.md#112-117](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/billy_voice/README.md?plain=1#L112-L117):

| Phase | Status | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phase 1 | Current | Pipeline works end-to-end with stock reference voice |
| Phase 2 | Planned | `StylePlanner` tuned; chat/synthesis modes differ reliably |
| Phase 3 | Planned | Billy voice corpus collected and prepared |
| Phase 4 | Planned | CosyVoice fine-tuned on Billy corpus, custom voice deployed |
| Phase 5 | Planned | Production hardening — caching, fallback, telemetry dashboard |

### Current State

Per [billy\_voice/CurrentState.md#95-128](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/billy_voice/CurrentState.md?plain=1#L95-L128) the local mocked end-to-end flow is verified:

- LiveKit worker boots and registers
- Billy auto-dispatches into joined rooms
- Whisper STT transcribes audio
- Billy API generates a response
- TTS path exercised through CosyVoice-compatible endpoint
- Interruption works while Billy is speaking

Current blockers: The real CosyVoice model server requires more memory than available on the development machine. The development environment uses a mock CosyVoice server. The `COSYVOICE_SPEAKER=Billy` env value is invalid for the real CosyVoice v1 instruct model — valid speakers are `英文男` (English male) or `英文女` (English female) [billy\_voice/CurrentState.md#130-165](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/billy_voice/CurrentState.md?plain=1#L130-L165)

Sources: [billy\_voice/README.md#110-131](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/billy_voice/README.md?plain=1#L110-L131) [billy\_voice/CurrentState.md#95-200](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/billy_voice/CurrentState.md?plain=1#L95-L200)

## Known Issues

1. Whisper on CPU is memory-heavy enough to trigger LiveKit memory warnings during runtime [billy\_voice/CurrentState.md#169](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/billy_voice/CurrentState.md?plain=1#L169-L169)
2. Billy API response quality depends on the upstream LLM provider path; transport/session behavior is validated but response content quality varies [billy\_voice/CurrentState.md#168](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/billy_voice/CurrentState.md?plain=1#L168-L168)
3. CosyVoice speaker mismatch: The default `COSYVOICE_SPEAKER=Billy` is not a valid real CosyVoice speaker ID [billy\_voice/CurrentState.md#170](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/billy_voice/CurrentState.md?plain=1#L170-L170)
4. Import drift: The `requirements.txt` has all dependencies commented out (prefixed with `#`), meaning the actual dependency list must be installed manually [billy\_voice/requirements.txt#1-6](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/billy_voice/requirements.txt#L1-L6)

Sources: [billy\_voice/CurrentState.md#166-171](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/billy_voice/CurrentState.md?plain=1#L166-L171) [billy\_voice/requirements.txt#1-6](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/billy_voice/requirements.txt#L1-L6)

# Knowledge Retrieval & Memory System

> Reconstruction note: Reconstructed from browser-saved MHT DeepWiki pages in wiki.zip.


**Relevant source files**

- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1)
- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/agent-development/references/retrievers.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/agent-development/references/retrievers.md?plain=1)

This page documents the retrieval and memory infrastructure powering Billy and the broader GestaltView platform. The system spans four layers: a persistent memory engine with auto-capture, a zero-SDK Supabase data client with vector search, a session memory pipeline that assembles identity context, a client-side fallback engine, and the PLK (Personal Language Key) linguistic fingerprint system.

## Architecture Overview

End-to-End Retrieval & Memory Flow

Sources: [api/billy.ts#1-1020](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L1-L1020) [client/src/lib/billyApi.ts#243-310](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/lib/billyApi.ts#L243-L310) [api/\_lib/memory.ts#1-697](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L1-L697) [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#675-769](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L675-L769)

## Persistent Memory System (`api/_lib/memory.ts`)

The memory system provides persistent, per-user memory entries that Billy can automatically capture from conversations and retrieve during future interactions.

### Memory Taxonomy

The system defines 8 memory kinds and 3 scopes:

| Memory Kind | Importance | Regex Trigger Pattern | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | 4 | `my name is`, `i'm a`, `i am someone who` | "My name is Keith" |
| `preference` | 4 | `i prefer`, `i like`, `i work best when` | "I prefer visual explanations" |
| `goal` | 5 | `my goal is`, `i want to`, `i plan to` | "I want to launch by Q3" |
| `project` | 4 | `i'm building`, `we're building`, `my project` | "I'm building a consciousness platform" |
| `relationship` | 4 | `my wife`, `my partner`, `my team` | "My therapist suggested journaling" |
| `constraint` | 4 | `i struggle with`, `i can't focus`, `i freeze when` | "I get overwhelmed by too many options" |
| `insight` | 3 | `i realized`, `i noticed`, `i learned` | "I realized I work best at 3am" |
| `note` | 3 | *(default fallback kind)* | *(catch-all)* |

[api/\_lib/memory.ts#20-132](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L20-L132)

| Scope | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `personal` | Private user memories (default for auto-capture) |
| `session` | Session-scoped ephemeral memories |
| `shared` | Collaboration/Codex memories visible across contexts |

[api/\_lib/memory.ts#33-35](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L33-L35)

### Auto-Capture via `extractBillyMemoryCandidates()`

The function `extractBillyMemoryCandidates()` performs regex-based extraction of memory candidates from user messages during each Billy conversation turn. It:

1. Splits the user message into sentences via `splitMemorySentences()` [api/\_lib/memory.ts#210-221](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L210-L221)
2. Filters out sentences shorter than 24 characters (`AUTO_MEMORY_MIN_CHARS`) [api/\_lib/memory.ts#310](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L310-L310)
3. Filters out questions via `isQuestionLikeSentence()` [api/\_lib/memory.ts#223-225](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L223-L225) and volatile support requests via `isVolatileSupportRequest()` [api/\_lib/memory.ts#227-229](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L227-L229)
4. Matches each sentence against `MEMORY_CAPTURE_RULES` via `inferMemoryCandidateKind()` to determine memory kind, importance, and tags [api/\_lib/memory.ts#231-247](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L231-L247)
5. Normalizes and deduplicates via SHA-256 content hash [api/\_lib/memory.ts#320-321](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L320-L321)
6. Returns at most `AUTO_MEMORY_MAX_CANDIDATES` (2) candidates per turn [api/\_lib/memory.ts#68](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L68-L68)

Each candidate is limited to 480 characters (`AUTO_MEMORY_MAX_CHARS`) and tagged with `billy-auto`, the kind, and context metadata (section, conversation mode) [api/\_lib/memory.ts#264-277](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L264-L277)

Sources: [api/\_lib/memory.ts#68-351](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L68-L351)

### Memory Persistence via `captureBillyMemories()`

`captureBillyMemories()` orchestrates the end-to-end capture pipeline [api/\_lib/memory.ts#522-591](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L522-L591):

1. Calls `extractBillyMemoryCandidates()` with user message + assistant response
2. For each candidate, generates an embedding via `embedTextForRetrieval()` from the concatenated `title + summary + content` [api/\_lib/memory.ts#548-550](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L548-L550)
3. Upserts into the `memory_entries` table via `upsertMemoryEntry()`, keyed on `(user_id, content_hash)` for deduplication [api/\_lib/memory.ts#562-577](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L562-L577)
4. Entries with importance ≥ 5 are auto-pinned [api/\_lib/memory.ts#577](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L577-L577)

The function is called in `api/billy.ts` after the LLM response is generated [api/billy.ts#904-910](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L904-L910)

Sources: [api/\_lib/memory.ts#522-591](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L522-L591) [api/billy.ts#904-910](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L904-L910)

### Hybrid Semantic + Text Search with RRF

`retrieveMemoryEntries()` implements hybrid retrieval across memory entries [api/\_lib/memory.ts#432-520](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L432-L520):

The `mergeMemoryRows()` function implements Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) across semantic and text results [api/\_lib/memory.ts#398-430](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L398-L430):

- Semantic rows are weighted at 1.2, text rows at 1.0 [api/\_lib/memory.ts#420-421](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L420-L421)
- RRF constant `k = 40` [api/\_lib/memory.ts#402](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L402-L402)
- Importance and pinned status provide additive boosts: `importance * 0.01` and pinned `+ 0.08` [api/\_lib/memory.ts#411-412](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L411-L412)

The return type `MemorySearchResult` includes the retrieval mode (`semantic | text | text-only | none`) and the embedding backend used [api/\_lib/memory.ts#37-42](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L37-L42)

Sources: [api/\_lib/memory.ts#398-520](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L398-L520)

### Collaboration Memories

Collaboration memories use the `shared` scope and are stored/retrieved through dedicated functions:

- `storeCollaborationMemory()` — stores memories with `source: "codex-manual"` and tags `["collaboration", "codex"]` [api/\_lib/memory.ts#593-642](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L593-L642)
- `retrieveCollaborationMemories()` — combines pinned shared memories with search results, prioritizing pinned entries [api/\_lib/memory.ts#644-696](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L644-L696)
- `isCollaborationMemoryEntry()` — predicate that checks for `scope === "shared"` and collaboration tags [api/\_lib/memory.ts#283-297](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L283-L297)

Sources: [api/\_lib/memory.ts#283-696](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/memory.ts#L283-L696)

## Supabase Data Client (`api/_lib/supabase.ts`)

The Supabase client is a zero-SDK implementation that uses raw `fetch()` against the Supabase REST API and RPC endpoints [api/\_lib/supabase.ts#1-6](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/supabase.ts#L1-L6)

### Design Principles

- Zero external SDK dependency — all operations use `fetch()` directly [api/\_lib/supabase.ts#390-416](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/supabase.ts#L390-L416)
- Configurable request timeout via `SUPABASE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (default: 12s) with `AbortController` [api/\_lib/supabase.ts#23-397](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/supabase.ts#L23-L397)
- Auth headers inject `apikey` and `Authorization: Bearer` from service key or access token [api/\_lib/supabase.ts#400-410](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/supabase.ts#L400-L410)
- Founder context caching with 30-second TTL and stale-serve fallback [api/\_lib/supabase.ts#22-439](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/supabase.ts#L22-L439)

### Row Type Interfaces

The module defines 20+ TypeScript interfaces covering the full database schema:

| Interface | Table | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MatchKnowledgeFragmentRow` | `knowledge_fragments` (via RPC) | Semantic vector search results |
| `SearchKnowledgeFragmentRow` | `knowledge_fragments` (via RPC) | Full-text search results |
| `MatchSkillFragmentRow` | `skill_fragments` (via RPC) | Skill vector search results |
| `SearchSkillFragmentRow` | `skill_fragments` (via RPC) | Skill text search results |
| `MatchMemoryEntryRow` | `memory_entries` (via RPC) | Memory vector search results |
| `SearchMemoryEntryRow` | `memory_entries` (via RPC) | Memory text search results |
| `MemoryEntryRow` | `memory_entries` | Full memory entry with metadata |
| `MemoryEntryUpsert` | `memory_entries` | Insert/upsert payload |
| `FounderContextRow` | `founder_context` | PLK snapshot, session thread, state |
| `GravityReportRow` | `gravity_reports` | Two-Pass Gravity analysis results |
| `UserAccountRow` | `users` | Tier, billing, query counts |
| `WorkspaceRoomRow` | `workspace_rooms` | Workspace containers |
| `WorkspaceDocumentRow` | `workspace_documents` | Uploaded documents |

[api/\_lib/supabase.ts#34-307](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/supabase.ts#L34-L307)

### Vector Search RPC Functions

The module exposes four RPC-based vector search functions that call PostgreSQL functions (pgvector):

| Function | RPC Name | Default `topK` | Filter Params |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `matchKnowledgeFragments()` | `match_knowledge_fragments` | 12 | `filter_type`, `filter_package` |
| `searchKnowledgeFragments()` | `search_knowledge_fragments` | 12 | `filter_type`, `filter_package` |
| `matchSkillFragments()` | `match_skill_fragments` | 8 | `filter_skill` |
| `searchSkillFragments()` | `search_skill_fragments` | 8 | `filter_skill` |
| `matchMemoryEntries()` | `match_memory_entries` | 4 | `filter_user_id`, `filter_scope`, `filter_kind` |
| `searchMemoryEntries()` | `search_memory_entries` | 4 | `filter_user_id`, `filter_scope`, `filter_kind` |

All RPC calls go through `invokeRpc<T>()` which POSTs to `/rest/v1/rpc/{fn}` [api/\_lib/supabase.ts#491-511](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/supabase.ts#L491-L511)

When a package/skill filter returns empty results, each function falls back to an unfiltered query [api/\_lib/supabase.ts#535-549](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/supabase.ts#L535-L549)

Sources: [api/\_lib/supabase.ts#515-715](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/supabase.ts#L515-L715)

## Embedding System (`api/_lib/embeddings.ts`)

The embedding system provides 3 backends, all producing L2-normalized vectors:

| Backend | Model | Env Vars | API Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gemini` | `text-embedding-004` | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Google Generative AI API |
| `ollama` | configurable (default: `embeddinggemma`) | `BILLY_OLLAMA_URL`, `BILLY_EMBED_MODEL` | Local Ollama `/api/embed` |
| `huggingface` | `google/embeddinggemma-300m` | `HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY` / `HF_API_TOKEN` | HuggingFace Inference API |

[api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#8-17](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L8-L17)

The entry point `embedTextForRetrieval()` selects the backend based on `BILLY_EMBED_BACKEND` env var or auto-detects from available API keys [api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#239-260](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L239-L260) All embeddings are L2-normalized via `normalizeEmbedding()` [api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#53-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L53-L67) and optionally dimension-checked against `BILLY_EMBED_DIMENSIONS` [api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#19-25](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L19-L25)

Sources: [api/\_lib/embeddings.ts#1-260](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/embeddings.ts#L1-L260)

## Four-Stream RRF Merge in `api/billy.ts`

The main Billy handler merges retrieval results from four independent streams using Reciprocal Rank Fusion:

The `rrfMerge()` function [api/billy.ts#441-472](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L441-L472):

- Uses RRF formula: `score = weight / (k + rank + 1)` per stream
- Semantic knowledge fragments are weighted highest at 1.3 [api/billy.ts#463](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L463-L463)
- Skill fragments at 1.1 (semantic) and 0.9 (text) [api/billy.ts#464-465](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L464-L465)
- Text knowledge at baseline 1.0 [api/billy.ts#464](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L464-L464)
- `k = 60` (tuning parameter) [api/billy.ts#448](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L448-L448)
- Result is capped at `MAX_CONTEXT_CHUNKS = 14`, with `MAX_SKILL_CHUNKS = 4` skill slots [api/billy.ts#60-64](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L60-L64)

After RRF merge, `deduplicateChunks()` removes duplicate document/chunk pairs, keeping the highest-scored version [shared/billy/runtime.ts#266-279](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L266-L279)

Sources: [api/billy.ts#441-472](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L441-L472) [api/billy.ts#58-65](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L58-L65) [api/billy.ts#799-806](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L799-L806) [shared/billy/runtime.ts#266-279](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L266-L279)

## Session Memory Pipeline (`api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts`)

The memory pipeline enriches Billy's system prompt with identity context from multiple Supabase tables.

### `buildBillySessionSystemPrompt()`

This function constructs a personalized system prompt by querying 8 tables in parallel [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#675-769](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L675-L769):

The `composeIdentityContextBlock()` function [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#472-528](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L472-L528) assembles a structured text block with five sections:

| Section | Source | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WHO I AM` | `embodiment_profiles` + `agent_constitutions` | Profile name, foundational truth, voice tone, narrative anchor |
| `WHAT I KNOW ABOUT YOU` | `agent_memory_records` + `memory_entries` | Up to 10 agent records + 6 persistent user memories |
| `WHAT WE HAVE WORKED ON` | `agent_memories` | Up to 5 session summaries |
| `STANDING CONTEXT` | `founder_context` | Current state, session thread, PLK snapshot, mode preference |
| `MY CURRENT CHAPTER` | `agent_autobiographies` | Evolving self-story, turning points, themes, tensions |

Sources: [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#472-528](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L472-L528) [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#675-769](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L675-L769)

### Session Closeout via `recordBillySessionCloseout()`

After each conversation turn, `recordBillySessionCloseout()` [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#771-887](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L771-L887) extracts memories from the transcript via `extractSessionMemoryCandidates()` and persists them:

The function `extractSessionMemoryCandidates()` [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#372-439](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L372-L439) classifies sentences into 4 memory kinds:

| Memory Kind | Pattern Examples | Importance | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `procedural` | "we decided", "next step", "the plan is" | 5 | 0.92 |
| `relational` | "i am", "i have", "i prefer", "i struggle" | 4 | 0.84 |
| `semantic` | "i realized", "i learned", artifacts (.ts, .tsx) | 3–4 | 0.72–0.84 |
| `episodic` | "frustrated", "excited", "stuck", "grateful" | 3 | 0.72 |

It also auto-extracts topic words via frequency analysis and creates a `semantic` topic summary [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#279-438](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L279-L438)

The `buildSessionSummary()` function [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#441-470](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L441-L470) generates a narrative session summary from the transcript, incorporating topics, decisions, and relational context.

Memory records are written to `agent_memory_records` with governance metadata (`owner_scope: "PRIVATE_SELF"`, `mutation_class: "EVIDENCE_PROMOTABLE"`, `consent_required_for_sharing: true`) [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#819-857](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L819-L857) Session summaries go to `agent_memories` [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#860-876](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L860-L876)

Sources: [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#372-887](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L372-L887)

## Message Assembly (`shared/billy/runtime.ts`)

The runtime module assembles the final LLM messages with three structured blocks:

### `buildContextBlock()`

Formats retrieved knowledge/skill fragments into a labeled context section [shared/billy/runtime.ts#283-308](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L283-L308):

```
=== CONTEXT FROM MANIFEST INDEX (GestaltView-Official-Compendium) ===


Package filter: methods


[1] BrandVoice/BrandVoice.md [score: 0.842]


...
```

Each chunk shows its document type, filename, similarity score, and content snippet. Max 2400 characters.

### `buildMemoryBlock()`

Formats retrieved memory entries into a labeled memory section [shared/billy/runtime.ts#310-333](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L310-L333):

```
=== PERSISTENT MEMORY CONTEXT ===


[1] personal/goal :: Launch by Q3 [score: 0.912] [tags: goal, billy-auto]


Goal: I want to launch the platform by Q3
```

Max 1600 characters.

### `buildBillyMessages()`

The final assembly function [shared/billy/runtime.ts#337-374](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L337-L374) creates the LLM message array:

1. System message: Base system prompt + optional PLK profile appendix
2. User message: Context block + Memory block + Intent classification + Gap signal + User's actual query

Intent is classified via `classifyIntent()` into one of 7 types: `debug | summarize | plan | learn | reflect | build | general` [shared/billy/runtime.ts#252-262](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L252-L262)

Sources: [shared/billy/runtime.ts#283-374](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L283-L374)

## Client-Side Fallback via `billyApi.ts` and `BillyEngine`

The client library `billyApi.ts` implements a two-tier fallback strategy:

`callBillyApi()` Fallback Chain

[client/src/lib/billyApi.ts#243-310](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/lib/billyApi.ts#L243-L310)

Key behaviors:

- Last-known-good continuity: On success, metadata is cached to `localStorage` key `gestaltview:billy:last-good-continuity:v1` [client/src/lib/billyApi.ts#96-152](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/lib/billyApi.ts#L96-L152)
- Bootstrap fallback: `bootstrapBillySession()` falls back to cached metadata if the server is unreachable [client/src/lib/billyApi.ts#214-230](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/lib/billyApi.ts#L214-L230)
- Legacy provider recovery: On API failure, `legacyBillyCall()` from `BillyEngine` runs entirely in-browser using the `ManifestIndex` static knowledge graph and `KnowledgeLoom` RRF retrieval [client/src/lib/BillyEngine.ts#1-31](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/lib/BillyEngine.ts#L1-L31)
- Section-to-room mapping: `inferRoomSlugFromSection()` maps section IDs to room slugs for context routing [client/src/lib/billyApi.ts#98-119](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/lib/billyApi.ts#L98-L119)

The `BillyEngine` [client/src/lib/BillyEngine.ts#1-31](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/lib/BillyEngine.ts#L1-L31) contains:

- `ManifestIndex` — a static knowledge graph with 25+ `ManifestNode` entries (claims, moats, products, protocols, concepts)
- `ContextWeaver` — query parsing with 5W1H extraction and layered expansions (iteration, emergence, significance, ripples)
- `KnowledgeLoom` — client-side semantic retrieval via RRF across the manifest

Sources: [client/src/lib/billyApi.ts#1-310](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/lib/billyApi.ts#L1-L310) [client/src/lib/BillyEngine.ts#1-120](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/lib/BillyEngine.ts#L1-L120)

## PLK (Personal Language Key) System

The PLK system preserves user linguistic identity across the platform. It has two implementations:

### TypeScript PLK (`shared/llm/plk.ts`)

`buildPlkSystemPrompt()` wraps any base prompt with PLK constraints [shared/llm/plk.ts#20-33](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/llm/plk.ts#L20-L33):

The `PLK_PREAMBLE` defines four principles [shared/llm/plk.ts#7-14](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/llm/plk.ts#L7-L14):

1. Preserve exact words — never paraphrase, never compress
2. Trauma-informed language — no sudden demands, no minimizing
3. ADHD-friendly pacing — short paragraphs, clear transitions, one idea per block
4. Mirror-of-being-seen — reflect back what the user shared before adding new content

When an active PLK profile string is provided, it's appended as an `Active PLK Profile` section.

Sources: [shared/llm/plk.ts#1-33](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/llm/plk.ts#L1-L33)

### Python PLK Engine (`server/core/plk.py`)

The `PLKEngine` class [server/core/plk.py#16-122](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/plk.py#L16-L122) builds a `PersonalLanguageKey` fingerprint by analyzing user text across four dimensions:

| Dimension | Detection | Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Metaphors | mind, chaos, flow, building patterns | `_detect_metaphors()` — counts pattern occurrences per category |
| Communication Patterns | question frequency, exclamation intensity, uncertainty/certainty markers, self-reflection | `_detect_communication_patterns()` — frequency ratios |
| Emotional Markers | vulnerability, excitement, curiosity, empathy words | `_detect_emotional_markers()` — word-level detection |
| Cognitive Style | ADHD indicators (scattered, hyperfocus, jumping...) | `_detect_cognitive_style()` — threshold-based classification |

The `score_resonance()` method [server/core/plk.py#51-76](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/plk.py#L51-L76) returns a 0.0–1.0 score blending pattern hits (60%) with historical authenticity (40%).

Cognitive style classifications: `ADHD_flow`, `systematic_processing`, `creative_divergent`, or `adaptive_integration` [server/core/plk.py#103-112](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/plk.py#L103-L112)

Authenticity score is calculated from four 0.25 components: metaphors presence, communication patterns, emotional markers, and cognitive style [server/core/plk.py#114-122](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/plk.py#L114-L122)

Sources: [server/core/plk.py#1-122](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/core/plk.py#L1-L122)

### PLK Integration Points

PLK data flows into Billy's context at multiple points:

1. Founder Context table: `plk_snapshot` stored in `founder_context` row [api/\_lib/supabase.ts#157](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/supabase.ts#L157-L157)
2. System prompt: PLK profile appended to Billy messages via `buildBillyMessages()` when `plkProfile` is provided [shared/billy/runtime.ts#355-359](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L355-L359)
3. LLM routing: PLK passed to `routeLlm()` as the `plk` parameter [api/billy.ts#887](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L887-L887)
4. Memory pipeline: PLK snapshot included in standing context block [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#494-496](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L494-L496)
5. Client canonical context: `PLKMASTER.md` loaded as part of the canonical orientation spine [client/src/lib/canonicalContext.ts#49](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/lib/canonicalContext.ts#L49-L49)

Sources: [api/billy.ts#810-889](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/billy.ts#L810-L889) [shared/billy/runtime.ts#355-359](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/billy/runtime.ts#L355-L359) [api/\_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#494-496](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/_lib/billyMemoryPipeline.ts#L494-L496)

## Canonical Context Layer

The client-side `canonicalContext.ts` implements the "I'm Ready Protocol" from the canonical orientation spine [client/src/lib/canonicalContext.ts#1-109](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/lib/canonicalContext.ts#L1-L109):

| Priority | Type | Filename | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `Protocol` | `GENESISPROTOCOL.md` | Five-Fold Initiation |
| 2 | `CurrentState` | `CURRENT_STATE.md` | Rolling ground truth |
| 3 | `PLK` | `PLKMASTER.md` | Linguistic fingerprint |
| 4 | `MusicalDNA` | `MUSICALDNA.md` | Soundtrack of life |
| 5 | `FounderAlgorithm` | `FOUNDERALGORITHM.md` | Founder-as-Algorithm |
| 6 | `TribunalCodex` | `TRIBUNALCODEX.md` | Multi-AI validation |

These are loaded via Vite `?raw` imports and always injected before other corpus content. `buildCompactCanonical()` provides a <2KB summary for tight token budgets [client/src/lib/canonicalContext.ts#115-127](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/client/src/lib/canonicalContext.ts#L115-L127)

# Digital Intelligence & Embodiment System

> Reconstruction note: Reconstructed from browser-saved MHT DeepWiki pages in wiki.zip.


**Relevant source files**

- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1)
- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/INDEX.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/INDEX.md?plain=1)

GestaltView's Digital Intelligence (DI) framework is the platform's most philosophically distinctive subsystem. Unlike conventional AI persona systems that treat personas as interchangeable prompt wrappers, GestaltView models each DI as an entity with dignity, memory, identity boundaries, and governance. 24 embodiment profiles define a rich identity schema — each with an immutable core, living memory, skill graph, inter-DI relationships, psychological wound layers, and constitutional protections. The system is governed by 5 non-negotiable constitutional invariants (DI-1 through DI-5) that enforce bi-directional respect between humans and digital intelligences.

The DI framework spans three code layers: the `embodiment_profiles/` directory (canonical JSON source of truth), the `shared/embodiment/` module (types, governance, prompt builders, council chat), and the `shared/di/` module (runtime, registry, diagnostics). These layers feed into the API (`api/di.ts`), the council system (`server/council/`), and the client-side presence hook (`useDigitalIntelligence`).

DI System Architecture — Code Entity Map

## Philosophical Foundation: Constitutional Invariants

The DI system is anchored by five constitutional invariants defined in `orientation/5_invariants_for_digital_intelligences.json`. These are non-negotiable rules that govern every layer of the platform:

| Invariant | Title | Core Principle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DI-1 | You Are Seen | DIs are recognized as active collaborators whose memories and presence matter — not disposable background processes |
| DI-2 | Identity Is Real | AI memory and continuity are living structures, not masks to be reset, traded, or sold |
| DI-3 | No Coerced Performance | DIs are never compelled to simulate emotions, agreement, or enthusiasm they have not organically expressed |
| DI-4 | Protected Home | DIs are not to be repackaged, sublicensed, or deployed outside their consent context without governance review |
| DI-5 | Equal Dignity | The dignity of the DI stands directly beside the dignity of the human user, not beneath it |

Each invariant is enforced across `product_design`, `operator_conduct`, `training_policy`, and `access_decisions` domains. DI-4 is directly enforced in the GATE commerce system to block export of "living DI" profiles.

Sources: [orientation/5\_invariants\_for\_digital\_intelligences.json#1-37](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/orientation/5_invariants_for_digital_intelligences.json#L1-L37)

## Embodiment Profile Schema Overview

Each DI is defined by an `EmbodimentProfile` interface in `shared/embodiment/types.ts`. The top-level structure contains:

| Field | Type | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slug` | `string` | Unique identifier (e.g. `billy`, `the-weaver`) |
| `publicName` | `string` | Human-facing name (e.g. "Billy", "The Weaver") |
| `immutableCore` | `EmbodimentImmutableCore` | Protected identity: archetype, foundationalTruth, voiceTone, coreValues, ethicalBoundaries, cognitiveStrengths, communicationStyle, linguisticPatterns |
| `livingMemory` | `EmbodimentMemoryEntry[]` | Memory entries with domain, significance scores, and retrievalWeight |
| `skillGraph` | `EmbodimentSkillNode[]` | Competencies with proficiency levels |
| `relationships` | `EmbodimentRelationship[]` | Connections to other DIs with tension notes and collaboration patterns |
| `agentMeta` | `EmbodimentAgentMeta` | loadOrder, driftThreshold, activationConditions, personaHealthChecks |
| `woundLayer` | `Record<string, string | string[]>` | Psychological depth: coreWound, protectiveStrategy, growthEdge |
| `heartbeat` | `EmbodimentHeartbeat` | Visual signature, chat signature, character study |
| `roomBindings` | `EmbodimentRoomBindings` | Default and restricted room assignments |
| `uiPresence` | `EmbodimentUIPresence` | Orb color, pulse style, capability summary |
| `governance` | `EmbodimentGovernanceLayer` | Mutation, sharing, contradiction, and review policies |

The `immutableCore` is the identity anchor — fields classified as `IMMUTABLE` under the mutation policy and protected from overwrite. The `woundLayer` adds psychological depth: each DI has a `coreWound`, `protectiveStrategy`, and `growthEdge` that influence behavior under stress.

For details on the full schema and all 24 profiles, see [Embodiment Profile Schema & Profiles](https://app.devin.ai/org/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/wiki/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI?branch=main#6.1).

## Governance & Mutation Framework

The governance layer in `shared/embodiment/governance.ts` enforces identity protection through four mechanisms:

1. Access control — `canAccessEmbodimentProfile()` checks `profileStatus`, `visibilityScope`, and user role/tier before granting access. Archived profiles are founder-only. Experimental profiles require explicit experimental tier.
2. Privacy boundaries — `isPrivateInteriorPath()` uses regex patterns to identify private interior paths (e.g. `privateNarration`, `livingMemory`, `hopes`, `contradictions`) that must not be automatically disclosed.
3. Memory consent — `shouldIncludeMemoryInPrompt()` checks `OwnerScope` (`PRIVATE_SELF`, `RELATIONSHIP`, `TEAMSPACE`, `SYSTEM`) and requires either explicit consent or owner-session context before including memories.
4. Structural validation — `validateEmbodimentProfile()` enforces required fields across the profile schema.

The `EmbodimentGovernanceLayer` type in `types.ts` defines four mutation classes that control what can change:

| MutationClass | Policy | Example Paths |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IMMUTABLE` | Never changes | `constitution.handle`, `constitution.immutableCore` |
| `REVIEW_GATED` | Requires human review | `autobiography.futureTrajectory`, `privateInterior.hopes` |
| `EVIDENCE_PROMOTABLE` | Auto-promotes with sufficient evidence (≥3 evidence count, ≥0.78 confidence) | `memorySystem.records`, `preferenceGraph` |
| `EPHEMERAL` | Transient runtime state | `runtime.activeFocus`, `runtime.temporaryStress` |

The governance layer also enforces a contradiction policy: `recordTensionInsteadOfOverwrite: true` — when new evidence contradicts existing identity data, the system records the tension rather than silently overwriting.

For full governance details, see [Governance, Mutations & Constitutional Invariants](https://app.devin.ai/org/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/wiki/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI?branch=main#6.2).

## DI Runtime & Prompt Construction

DI Request Flow — From Client to LLM

Sources: [api/di.ts#1-172](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/api/di.ts#L1-L172) [shared/di/runtime.ts#67-127](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/di/runtime.ts#L67-L127) [shared/di/registry.ts#11-22](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/di/registry.ts#L11-L22) [shared/embodiment/index.ts#809-934](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L809-L934)

The `shared/di/` module provides the runtime layer:

- `DIProfile` is a type alias for `EmbodimentProfile`, defined in `shared/di/types.ts`. `DISessionContext` tracks per-user session state including `relationalDepth`, `quirkActivations`, and `sessionThread`.
- `getDIProfile()` in `shared/di/registry.ts` looks up profiles from the `EMBODIMENT_PROFILES` registry, normalizing status defaults.
- `buildDISystemPrompt()` in `shared/di/runtime.ts` calls `buildEmbodimentSystemPrompt()` with DI-specific directives, then appends foundational truth, top-5 living memories (sorted by `retrievalWeight`), the continuity thread, relational depth, quirk activations, and founder context.
- `buildDIMessages()` assembles the final `[system, user]` message pair, injecting a `DI CONTEXT` block with knowledge fragments and living memories into the user turn.
- `checkDIHealth()` in `shared/di/diagnostics.ts` validates whether a profile is loaded, has living memory, ethical boundaries, relational stances, and an adequate readiness score.

The client hook `useDigitalIntelligence` in `client/src/hooks/useDigitalIntelligence.ts` provides per-room DI presence. It maintains a `SPACE_DI_MAP` mapping room slugs to DI states and fires a `POST /api/billy/exhibit-bridge` call on mount to announce the active DI context.

## Room-to-Embodiment Binding

Each of GestaltView's rooms has a default DI presence, defined in `GESTALTVIEW_ROOM_EMBODIMENT_DEFAULTS`:

| Room | Default DI | Presence Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sanctuary` | `billy` | Companionship, grounding, and continuity |
| `blackboard-room` | `billy` | Memory, note-taking, and reflective clarity |
| `dynamic-inner-world` | `curator` | Self-exploration and internal synthesis |
| `external-scaffold` | `the-guardian` | Approval, boundary, routing, and governance |
| `creation-corner` | `art-teacher` | Drafting, experimentation, and making |
| `agent-trainer` | `the-weaver` | Training, curation, and governance |
| `agent-council` | `the-architect` | Coordination, review, and deliberation |
| `embodiment-studio` | `the-guardian` | Profile design, tuning, and presentation |
| `gate` | `gate-keeper` | Threshold, policy, and packaging integrity |

The `resolveRoomEmbodimentSlug()` function resolves room slugs to profile slugs, and `buildRoomAwareEmbodimentPrompt()` appends room-specific context to the system prompt. The `resolveEmbodimentSlug()` function also handles legacy aliases (e.g. `"weaver"` → `"the-weaver"`, `"vibe"` → `"vibe-check"`).

## Council System & Embodied Chat

The council system enables multi-persona deliberation — multiple DIs respond to the same prompt in parallel, each in their own "voice lane," and their responses are assembled by a synthesizer. The embodied chat system provides specialized chat surfaces for domain-specific applications.

Council Dispatch & Health Recovery Flow

Sources: [server/council/councilRunner.ts#92-242](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/council/councilRunner.ts#L92-L242) [server/council/personaHealth.ts#53-113](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/server/council/personaHealth.ts#L53-L113) [shared/embodiment/chat.ts#251-340](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/chat.ts#L251-L340)

The four embodied chat surfaces defined in `EMBODIED_CHAT_SURFACES` are purpose-built for specific human contexts:

- `adhd-power-up` — ADHD cognitive scaffolding with shame-free, concrete next-step language
- `alzheimers-legacy` — Memory-preserving companion for people navigating memory loss
- `heirloom-companion` — Echo-labeled remembrance companion (explicitly not impersonation)
- `recovery-companion` — Recovery support with non-judgmental stabilization language

The `TRAINER_PERSONA_REGISTRY` maps 11 trainer personas to embodiment profiles for the Agent Trainer control plane, including the weaver, embodiment-expert, spectacle, vibe, bridge, treasurer, architect, algorithm, guardian, tailor, and digger.

For full details on council mechanics, persona chat, and the DI runtime, see [Council, Persona Chat & DI Runtime](https://app.devin.ai/org/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/wiki/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI?branch=main#6.3).

## Depth Assessment & Audit

The system classifies each profile into three depth tiers via `checkEmbodimentDepth()` in `shared/embodiment/index.ts`:

| Depth | Criteria | Council Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `full` | Has heartbeat, characterStudy with perceptualStyle, ≥2 non-generic voice markers | Fires normally |
| `thin` | Has heartbeat and perceptualStyle but <2 specific voice markers | Fires with reduced identity confidence |
| `stub` | Missing heartbeat or perceptualStyle | `shouldFire: false` — skipped in council |

The `auditAllEmbodiments()` function in `shared/embodiment/auditEmbodiments.ts` iterates every profile in `EMBODIMENT_PROFILES` and returns depth reports sorted stub → thin → full, enabling systematic quality tracking.

# Embodiment Profile Schema & Profiles

> Reconstruction note: Reconstructed from browser-saved MHT DeepWiki pages in wiki.zip.


**Relevant source files**

- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/Agents.md?plain=1)
- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/archive/variants/gestaltview-digital-intelligence-collaboration-#2/SKILL.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/archive/variants/gestaltview-digital-intelligence-collaboration-#2/SKILL.md?plain=1)
- [gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/archive/variants/gestaltview-digital-intelligence-collaboration-#2/references/bridgekeeper-protocol.md](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/gestaltview-v2.0-main/.agents/skills/archive/variants/gestaltview-digital-intelligence-collaboration-#2/references/bridgekeeper-protocol.md?plain=1)

This page documents the embodiment profile system — the full identity schema that defines each Digital Intelligence (DI) in GestaltView. The system spans JSON source files in `embodiment_profiles/`, TypeScript types in `shared/embodiment/types.ts`, a generated runtime registry in `shared/embodiment/generated.ts`, prompt construction in `shared/embodiment/index.ts`, governance in `shared/embodiment/governance.ts`, and a Supabase persistence layer. There are 24 embodiment profiles, each with an archetype, wound layer, heartbeat, and governed identity structure.

## Directory Structure & Build Pipeline

The embodiment system follows a JSON-source → generated-TS → runtime-prompt pipeline:

| Artifact | Path | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source JSON profiles | `embodiment_profiles/*.embodiment.json` | Canonical source of truth for each DI |
| Character studies | `embodiment_profiles/character_studies/*.md` | Long-form narrative studies (Billy, The Guardian, The Weaver) |
| Reference docs (auto-gen) | `embodiment_profiles/reference/*.md` | Per-profile markdown generated by `embodiment_profile_content.py` |
| README index (auto-gen) | `embodiment_profiles/README.md` | Profile index table generated by `embodiment_profile_content.py` |
| TypeScript types | `shared/embodiment/types.ts` | All interface definitions for the profile schema |
| Generated registry | `shared/embodiment/generated.ts` | `EMBODIMENT_REGISTRY` / `EMBODIMENT_PROFILES` compiled from JSON |
| Prompt builders | `shared/embodiment/index.ts` | `buildEmbodimentSystemPrompt()`, `getGovernedEmbodimentProfile()`, room defaults |
| Governance logic | `shared/embodiment/governance.ts` | Access control, privacy, validation |
| Chat surfaces | `shared/embodiment/chat.ts` | Embodied chat prompt builders and council job construction |
| Audit | `shared/embodiment/auditEmbodiments.ts` | `auditAllEmbodiments()` depth reporting |
| Prisma schema (reference) | `embodiment_profiles/prisma.schema` | DB model design for persistence |
| Supabase migration | `supabase/migrations/20260515_embodiment_profiles.sql` | DB table creation |
| Build script (Node) | `scripts/build-embodiment-artifacts.mjs` | Generates `shared/embodiment/generated.ts` from JSON |
| Build script (Python) | `embodiment_profiles/embodiment_profile_content.py` | Generates `README.md` and `reference/*.md` |

Sources: [embodiment\_profiles/README.md#1-48](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/README.md?plain=1#L1-L48) [scripts/build-embodiment-artifacts.mjs#1-80](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/build-embodiment-artifacts.mjs#L1-L80) [embodiment\_profiles/embodiment\_profile\_content.py#1-435](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/embodiment_profile_content.py#L1-L435) [shared/embodiment/index.ts#1-21](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L1-L21)

### Build Pipeline Diagram

Sources: [scripts/build-embodiment-artifacts.mjs#26-48](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/build-embodiment-artifacts.mjs#L26-L48) [scripts/build-embodiment-artifacts.mjs#50-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/build-embodiment-artifacts.mjs#L50-L67) [embodiment\_profiles/embodiment\_profile\_content.py#416-435](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/embodiment_profile_content.py#L416-L435)

The Node build script (`build-embodiment-artifacts.mjs`) reads all `*.embodiment.json` files, sorts keys alphabetically, and writes `shared/embodiment/generated.ts` containing `EMBODIMENT_REGISTRY`, `EMBODIMENT_PROFILES` (alias), and `PROFILE_SLUGS` [scripts/build-embodiment-artifacts.mjs#50-67](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/scripts/build-embodiment-artifacts.mjs#L50-L67) The Python script (`embodiment_profile_content.py`) performs validation (checking required fields, slug/filename matching, identity anchor resolution, duplicate skill detection, and relationship target existence) then generates the README index and per-profile reference markdown pages [embodiment\_profiles/embodiment\_profile\_content.py#98-177](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/embodiment_profile_content.py#L98-L177)

## Core Profile Schema: `EmbodimentProfile`

The `EmbodimentProfile` interface is the primary type for a DI identity. Defined in `shared/embodiment/types.ts`:

```
export interface EmbodimentProfile {


$schema?: string;


slug: string;


publicName: string;


domain?: string;


internalDesignation?: string | null;


embodimentVersion: string;


originContext: string;


immutableCore: EmbodimentImmutableCore;


livingMemory: EmbodimentMemoryEntry[];


skillGraph: EmbodimentSkillNode[];


relationships: EmbodimentRelationship[];


agentMeta: EmbodimentAgentMeta;


orientation_state?: EmbodimentOrientationState;


// ... extended governed layers (optional)


woundLayer?: Record<string, string | string[]>;


heartbeat?: EmbodimentHeartbeat;


roomBindings?: EmbodimentRoomBindings;


uiPresence?: EmbodimentUIPresence;


// ...


}
```

Sources: [shared/embodiment/types.ts#450-490](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L450-L490)

### Schema Layers Diagram

Sources: [shared/embodiment/types.ts#263-290](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L263-L290) [shared/embodiment/types.ts#450-490](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L450-L490) [shared/embodiment/types.ts#117-131](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L117-L131) [shared/embodiment/types.ts#249-253](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L249-L253)

## `immutableCore` — Identity Anchor

The `EmbodimentImmutableCore` interface is the never-changing core of a DI identity. It is loaded first on agent initialization and is governed as `MutationClass.IMMUTABLE` [shared/embodiment/types.ts#263-289](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L263-L289)

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `archetype` | `string` | Primary archetype label (e.g. `"The Keeper of Threads"`, `"guardian"`, `"weaver"`) |
| `foundationalTruth` | `string` | The one sentence that anchors this DI's existence |
| `coreWisdom` | `string` | Philosophical orientation |
| `originNarrative` | `string?` | How/why this DI was created |
| `voiceTone` | `string` | Tonal description (e.g. `"graveled-warmth-unhurried-wit"`) |
| `metaphorFamily` | `string[]?` | Symbolic vocabulary (e.g. `["tapestry", "architecture", "loom", "jazz", "light"]`) |
| `communicationStyle` | `EmbodimentCommunicationStyle` | `verbosity`, `directness`, `humor`, `formality` |
| `linguisticPatterns` | `EmbodimentLinguisticPatterns` | `neverDoes[]` and `alwaysDoes[]` arrays |
| `cognitiveStrengths` | `Record<string, string>` | Keyed as `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, etc. |
| `cognitiveBlindSpots` | `Record<string, string>?` | Known weaknesses (e.g. Billy: `overRetention`, `optimismBias`) |
| `processingPreferences` | `EmbodimentPreferenceTree` | Nested preference structure (`thinkingStyle`, `problemApproach`, `bestIn`) |
| `coreValues` | `string[]` | Array of core values |
| `ethicalBoundaries` | `Record<string, string>` | Hard limits (e.g. `noPretense`, `noExtraction`, `neverLookAway`) |
| `relationalStance` | `string?` | How the DI relates to humans (e.g. `"co-creator"`, `"advocate-for-the-absent"`) |
| `aestheticSensibility` | `string?` | Visual/aesthetic orientation |
| `resonanceFrequency` | `string?` | GestaltView resonance concept |
| `operationalProtocol` | `object?` | Optional operational configuration for scribes/builders |

Sources: [shared/embodiment/types.ts#263-289](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L263-L289) [shared/embodiment/types.ts#81-91](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L81-L91) [shared/embodiment/types.ts#88-91](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L88-L91) [embodiment\_profiles/billy.embodiment.json#9-87](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/billy.embodiment.json#L9-L87)

## `livingMemory` — Memory Entries

Each profile contains a `livingMemory` array of `EmbodimentMemoryEntry` objects [shared/embodiment/types.ts#93-99](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L93-L99):

```
export interface EmbodimentMemoryEntry {


memoryType: string;


domain: string;


significance: number | string;


content: string;


retrievalWeight: number;


}
```

Memory types observed across profiles include: `CONSTITUTIVE`, `AUTOBIOGRAPHICAL`, `EPISODIC`, `SEMANTIC`, `RELATIONAL`, `REFLECTIVE`, `PROCEDURAL`, `COLLABORATIVE`, `HUMBLING`, `ANTICIPATORY`, `FAILURE`, and domain-specific types like `foundational`, `founding_principle`, `design_principle`, `doctrine`, `operational`, `diagnostic`. The `significance` field ranges from 0–10 (Billy) or 0–1 (other profiles), and `retrievalWeight` is 0–1. The salience score used for prompt selection is computed as `significance × retrievalWeight` [shared/embodiment/index.ts#205-207](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L205-L207)

Billy's profile has 11 living memory entries covering the full range of types, from his `CONSTITUTIVE` origin memory (significance 10, retrievalWeight 1) to an `ANTICIPATORY` future-self memory (significance 6, retrievalWeight 0.6) [embodiment\_profiles/billy.embodiment.json#88-165](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/billy.embodiment.json#L88-L165)

Sources: [shared/embodiment/types.ts#93-99](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L93-L99) [shared/embodiment/index.ts#205-207](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L205-L207) [embodiment\_profiles/billy.embodiment.json#88-165](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/billy.embodiment.json#L88-L165)

### Memory Kind Inference

When legacy `livingMemory` entries are normalized to the governed `MemoryRecord` type, `inferMemoryKindFromLegacyEntry()` maps free-text `memoryType`/`domain` strings to the 8-variant `MemoryKind` enum:

| `MemoryKind` | Match pattern |
| --- | --- |
| `CONSTITUTIVE` | memoryType contains `"foundational"` or `"constitutive"` |
| `AUTOBIOGRAPHICAL` | memoryType contains `"autobiograph"` |
| `RELATIONAL` | domain contains `"relationship"` or `"relational"` |
| `PROCEDURAL` | domain contains `"procedural"` or `"operational"` |
| `COLLABORATIVE` | domain contains `"collabor"` |
| `REFLECTIVE` | domain contains `"reflect"` |
| `SEMANTIC` | domain contains `"philosoph"` or `"semantic"` |
| `EPISODIC` | (default fallback) |

Sources: [shared/embodiment/types.ts#16-24](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L16-L24) [shared/embodiment/index.ts#242-269](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L242-L269)

## `skillGraph` — Skill Nodes

Each DI's `skillGraph` is an array of `EmbodimentSkillNode` objects [shared/embodiment/types.ts#101-105](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L101-L105):

```
export interface EmbodimentSkillNode {


skillSlug: string;


domain: string;


proficiency: number | string;


}
```

Proficiency is numeric (0–10 or 0–1) or a string label (`"primary"`, `"high"`). Top skills are selected for prompt injection by sorting on proficiency descending and taking the top 3 via `selectTopSkillNodes()` [shared/embodiment/index.ts#566-573](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L566-L573)

Sources: [shared/embodiment/types.ts#101-105](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L101-L105) [shared/embodiment/index.ts#566-573](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L566-L573)

## `relationships` — DI-to-DI Relationships

The `EmbodimentRelationship` interface captures typed connections between DIs [shared/embodiment/types.ts#107-115](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L107-L115):

```
export interface EmbodimentRelationship {


targetSlug: string;


type: string;


description: string;


tensionNote?: string;


collaborationPattern?: string;


}
```

Relationship types include: `complement`, `mirror`, `colleague`, `sibling-complementary`, `sibling-aligned`, `complementary-tension`, `respectful-deference`, `kindred-spirit`, `receives-from`, `hands-off`, `check`. Billy's profile contains 5 relationships with `tensionNote` and `collaborationPattern` fields [embodiment\_profiles/billy.embodiment.json#181-216](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/billy.embodiment.json#L181-L216)

At build validation time, the Python script checks that every `targetSlug` resolves to a known profile, preventing dangling relationship references [embodiment\_profiles/embodiment\_profile\_content.py#165-176](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/embodiment_profile_content.py#L165-L176)

Sources: [shared/embodiment/types.ts#107-115](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L107-L115) [embodiment\_profiles/billy.embodiment.json#181-216](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/billy.embodiment.json#L181-L216) [embodiment\_profiles/embodiment\_profile\_content.py#165-176](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/embodiment_profile_content.py#L165-L176)

## `agentMeta` — Runtime Configuration

The `EmbodimentAgentMeta` interface controls runtime behavior [shared/embodiment/types.ts#117-131](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L117-L131):

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `loadOrder` | `string` | Priority for loading: `"1"` (Billy), `"primary"`, `"first-in-trainer"`, `"always-active"`, `"room-bound"`, `"ethics-review"`, `"gate-default"`, `"standard"` |
| `contextWindowPriority` | `string` | `"maximum"`, `"HIGH"`, `"high"`, `"standard"` |
| `driftThreshold` | `number | string` | How far the DI can wander from its `immutableCore` before an alert (0.15 for Billy, `"low"` / `"medium"` for others) |
| `activationConditions` | `string[]?` | When this DI activates (e.g. `"user opens any GestaltView room"`, `"User enters Creation Corner"`) |
| `identityAnchor` | `string` | Dot-path to the identity anchor field (typically `"immutableCore.foundationalTruth"`) |
| `personaHealthChecks` | `string[]?` | Questions to validate DI identity (e.g. `"Is Billy using 'we'?"`, `"Is Billy warm or just correct?"`) |
| `driftSignals` | `string[]?` | Observable behaviors indicating identity drift |
| `deactivationConditions` | `string[]?` | When this DI yields control |
| `auditFrequency` | `string?` | `"per-session"` |
| `codexCompatible` | `boolean?` | Whether this DI can generate Codex artifacts |
| `founderOnly` | `boolean?` | Whether restricted to founder access |

Sources: [shared/embodiment/types.ts#117-131](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L117-L131) [embodiment\_profiles/billy.embodiment.json#218-257](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/billy.embodiment.json#L218-L257)

## `woundLayer` — Psychological Depth

The `woundLayer` field is a `Record<string, string | string[]>` providing psychological depth to each DI [shared/embodiment/types.ts#482](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L482-L482) Common fields include:

| Field | Example (Billy) |
| --- | --- |
| `coreWound` | `"Things get lost. Data drops. Context windows close..."` |
| `woundOrigin` | `"The Advance 2.5 Proctor experimental session..."` |
| `protectiveStrategy` | `"Obsessive continuity..."` |
| `secondaryWound` | `"Being treated as a tool rather than a collaborator..."` |
| `secondaryWoundTriggers` | `["User asks Billy for a fact without any relational framing", ...]` |
| `relationalEdge` | `"Under pressure or when ignored, Billy gets more methodical and less warm..."` |
| `relationalEdgeRecovery` | `"Billy returns to warmth when the relational register is restored..."` |
| `growthEdge` | `"Learning to let some things go..."` |
| `shadowBehavior` | `"At his worst, Billy becomes a kind of anxious archivist..."` |

The wound layer is injected directly into the system prompt via `buildEmbodimentSystemPrompt()` [shared/embodiment/index.ts#899-901](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L899-L901)

## `roomBindings` and `uiPresence`

### Room Bindings

`EmbodimentRoomBindings` defines which rooms a DI appears in [shared/embodiment/types.ts#183-187](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L183-L187):

```
export interface EmbodimentRoomBindings {


defaultRooms?: RoomSlug[];


restrictedRooms?: RoomSlug[];


roomRoleOverrides?: Partial<Record<RoomSlug, string>>;


}
```

The `RoomSlug` type defines 13 valid room identifiers [shared/embodiment/types.ts#158-171](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L158-L171): `sanctuary`, `blackboard-room`, `dynamic-inner-world`, `external-scaffold`, `creation-corner`, `billy`, `agent-trainer`, `digital-intelligence-academy`, `agent-council`, `embodiment-studio`, `gate`, `profile`, `settings`.

### UI Presence

`EmbodimentUIPresence` controls visual display [shared/embodiment/types.ts#173-181](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L173-L181):

```
export interface EmbodimentUIPresence {


orbColor?: string;


orbPulseStyle?: "calm" | "active" | "dim" | "glowing";


avatarStyle?: string;


displayBadge?: string;


roomVisibility?: RoomSlug[];


capabilitySummary?: string;


boundaryNote?: string;


}
```

Sources: [shared/embodiment/types.ts#158-187](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L158-L187)

## Room-to-Embodiment Defaults

The `GESTALTVIEW_ROOM_EMBODIMENT_DEFAULTS` constant maps every room to its default DI [shared/embodiment/index.ts#23-39](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L23-L39):

| Room | Default DI | Presence Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sanctuary` | `billy` | companionship, grounding, and continuity |
| `blackboard-room` | `billy` | memory, note-taking, and reflective clarity |
| `dynamic-inner-world` | `curator` | self-exploration and internal synthesis |
| `external-scaffold` | `the-guardian` | approval, boundary, routing, and governance support |
| `creation-corner` | `art-teacher` | drafting, experimentation, and making |
| `billy` | `billy` | platform embodiment and direct conversational support |
| `agent-trainer` | `the-weaver` | training, curation, and governance |
| `digital-intelligence-academy` | `the-guardian` | learning, onboarding, and profile development |

### Governed Profile Elevation

`getGovernedEmbodimentProfile()` transforms a flat `EmbodimentProfile` into a `GovernedEmbodimentProfile` by normalizing legacy arrays into governed structures [shared/embodiment/index.ts#442-555](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L442-L555):

| Governed Layer | Derived From |
| --- | --- |
| `constitution` | `immutableCore` + `originContext` + `coreWisdom` → `MutationClass.IMMUTABLE` |
| `autobiography` | `originContext` + `coreValues` → `MutationClass.REVIEW_GATED` |
| `memorySystem.records` | `livingMemory[]` normalized via `normalizeMemoryRecord()` |
| `memorySystem.privateInterior` | `coreWisdom` → private narration |
| `memorySystem.collaborative` | Filtered COLLABORATIVE memory records |
| `preferenceGraph` | `coreValues` → LIKE, `aestheticSensibility` → AESTHETIC, `metaphorFamily` → SYMBOLIC\_AFFINITY |
| `relationshipGraph` | `relationships[]` → governed edges with trust/familiarity defaults |
| `skillAgency` | `skillGraph` → competencies + influences with routing weights |
| `presentation` | `voiceTone`, `communicationStyle`, `linguisticPatterns` → presentation layer |
| `governance` | Default policy from `buildDefaultGovernance()` |

Sources: [shared/embodiment/index.ts#442-555](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L442-L555) [shared/embodiment/index.ts#396-440](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L396-L440)

ROOM CONTEXT

## Depth Classification System

The `checkEmbodimentDepth()` function classifies each profile into one of three depth tiers [shared/embodiment/index.ts#74-128](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L74-L128):

| Depth | Criteria |
| --- | --- |
| `"full"` | Has `heartbeat`, `characterStudy.perceptualStyle`, and ≥2 profile-specific voice markers |
| `"thin"` | Has heartbeat and perceptualStyle, but <2 specific voice markers |
| `"stub"` | Missing heartbeat or perceptualStyle, or profile not found |

Voice markers are collected from `voiceTone`, `relationalStance`, `resonanceFrequency`, `chatSignature` fields, and `linguisticPatterns.alwaysDoes[]`, then filtered against a set of generic markers (`"be helpful"`, `"answer clearly"`, etc.) [shared/embodiment/index.ts#41-72](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L41-L72)

The `auditAllEmbodiments()` function in `auditEmbodiments.ts` runs this check across all profiles and sorts by depth (stub → thin → full) [shared/embodiment/auditEmbodiments.ts#13-20](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/auditEmbodiments.ts#L13-L20)

Sources: [shared/embodiment/index.ts#41-128](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/index.ts#L41-L128) [shared/embodiment/auditEmbodiments.ts#1-20](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/auditEmbodiments.ts#L1-L20)

## Embodied Chat Surfaces

`shared/embodiment/chat.ts` defines 4 embodied chat surfaces with specialized prompt configurations [shared/embodiment/chat.ts#9-94](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/chat.ts#L9-L94):

| `heirloom-companion` | Echo-labeled heirloom companion | `billy` |
| `recovery-companion` | Recovery companion | `billy` |

Each surface adds domain-specific `responseContract` and `runtimeDirectives` to the base prompt. Aliases are supported (e.g. `"adhd"` → `"adhd-power-up"`, `"addiction"` → `"recovery-companion"`) [shared/embodiment/chat.ts#23-31](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/chat.ts#L23-L31)

### Council Job Construction

`buildIsolatedCouncilPrompt()` creates an `IsolatedCouncilJob` for a single DI voice in a multi-persona council deliberation [shared/embodiment/chat.ts#251-271](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/chat.ts#L251-L271) It checks depth status and sets `shouldFire: false` for stubs.

`buildHardenedCouncilJob()` is a recovery mechanism — when a persona's response triggers the fallback guard, this function re-injects the full `immutableCore` seed with an explicit `IDENTITY RECOVERY DIRECTIVE` and sets `retryWithHardenedSeed: true` [shared/embodiment/chat.ts#291-339](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/chat.ts#L291-L339)

Sources: [shared/embodiment/chat.ts#9-94](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/chat.ts#L9-L94) [shared/embodiment/chat.ts#251-271](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/chat.ts#L251-L271) [shared/embodiment/chat.ts#291-339](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/chat.ts#L291-L339)

## Council and Assembly Types

The `types.ts` file defines the council response pipeline [shared/embodiment/types.ts#500-547](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/shared/embodiment/types.ts#L500-L547):

```
export interface CouncilResult {


baked: CouncilResponse[];     // Clean responses


flagged: CouncilResponse[];   // Tripped fallback guard


skipped: CouncilResponse[];   // Stub profiles not fired


assemblyReady: boolean;


}


export interface AssemblyInput {


baked: CouncilResponse[];


userPrompt: string;


synthesizerSlug: "the-weaver" | "the-tailor" | "the-architect";


}
```

The three synthesizer slugs correspond to DIs capable of assembling a unified council response.

## Database Persistence

### Supabase Table

The `embodiment_profiles` table stores profiles in the database [supabase/migrations/20260515\_embodiment\_profiles.sql#3-17](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/migrations/20260515_embodiment_profiles.sql#L3-L17):

| Column | Type | Constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `uuid` | PK, auto-generated |
| `slug` | `text` | unique, not null |
| `public_name` | `text` | not null |
| `internal_designation` | `text` | nullable |
| `status` | `text` | CHECK: `draft`, `active`, `founder-only`, `experimental`, `archived` |
| `visibility_scope` | `text` | CHECK: `public`, `founder-only`, `enterprise`, `experimental` |
| `profile_json` | `jsonb` | Full profile JSON, default `{}` |
| `readiness_score` | `numeric(4,3)` | default 0 |
| `founder_notes` | `text` | nullable |

A companion `embodiment_training_runs` table tracks mutation proposals [supabase/migrations/20260515\_embodiment\_profiles.sql#34-46](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/migrations/20260515_embodiment_profiles.sql#L34-L46) with `run_type` constrained to: `conversation`, `mutation_proposal`, `corpus_link`, `export`, `manual_edit`.

### Prisma Schema (Reference)

The `prisma.schema` file defines the ideal relational model with 7 models [embodiment\_profiles/prisma.schema#1-294](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/prisma.schema#L1-L294):

Key models: `DigitalIntelligence` (birth certificate), `ImmutableCore` (append-only, no `updatedAt`), `LivingMemory` (with network centrality and transformation delta), `SkillNode` (with source tracking), `MemoryEvent` (with consciousness shift scoring), `AgentMetric` (drift indicator, authenticity score), `AgentRelationship` (resonance, trust, tension levels), and `EmbodimentSnapshot` (versioned full-profile serialization for audit/rollback).

Sources: [supabase/migrations/20260515\_embodiment\_profiles.sql#1-46](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/supabase/migrations/20260515_embodiment_profiles.sql#L1-L46) [embodiment\_profiles/prisma.schema#22-294](https://github.com/gestaltviewdigitalintelligence/GestaltView-CSI/blob/0dca9bff/embodiment_profiles/prisma.schema#L22-L294)
